full_judgment:
In an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the Order dated 6-3-2008 passed by the District Judge, Feni in Civil Revision No. 14 of 2006 rejecting the revisional application and affirming the order dated 20-2-2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Feni in Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1992 allowing the application filed by the decree holder for amending the execution process by excluding lands from the scheduled of the decree under execution should not be set aside and pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The present opposite parties and their predecessors-in-interest as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 24 of 1958 which was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 157 of 1.963 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali for partition. Subsequently out of a compromise some of the parties were transposed and the opposite party No. 1 and 2 of the instant revisional application were made defendant Nos. 12 and 12(ka) of the said suit. The trial Court decreed the suit on preliminary form on 30-1-1966, against which the defendants preferred Title Appeal No. 170 of 1966 before the District Judge, Feni the then Noakhali wherein the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 were made respondent Nos. 21 and 22 and the appeal was allowed and the suit was decreed on compromise. Thereafter pursuant to the preliminary decree the final decree was drawn on 20-8-1990 by the Subordinate Judge, Additional Court, Noakhali. Thereafter the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 i.e. the decree-holder defendant Nos.12 and 12(ka) and 2 others filed Execution Case being No.2 of 1992 for taking possession in the suit land on the basis of the aforesaid final decree. During pendency of the Execution Case the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 of the present revisional application sold certain properties from the suit property to the present petitioner in the years 1996, 1997 and 1998 by registered sale deeds as well as hand over the possession thereon. All on a sudden on 9-6-2006 the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 who filed, the aforesaid Execution Case filed an application in the said case for striking out the lands mentioned in the schedule of the application from the execution proceeding. In the application it has been stated that the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 of the present revisional application filed Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 impleading the defendant Nos.12 and 12(ka) i.e. the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants. Thereafter the parties executed a solenama and the suit was dismissed on compromise and, as such, the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 have no claim in the lands mentioned in the application for exclusion. The executing Court vide order dated 20-2-2006 allowed the same.

3. The present petitioners as bona fide purchasers of the property in question which was excluded from the executing proceeding filed an application on 9-3-2006 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the Executing Court for recalling the order dated 20-2-2006. The Executing Court vide order dated 12-3-2006 rejected the application on the ground that the petitioners are not party in the proceeding as such the application is not maintainable in the eye of law.

4. Being aggrieved the present petitioners moved revisional application before the District Judge, Feni being Civil Revisional No. 14 of 2006 and the same was heard and disposed of by the District Judge, Feni who vide the impugned judgment and order dismissed the revision on question of maintainability of the application made by 3rd party. Being aggrieved the petitioners moved before this Court resulting granting of leave to consider whether the Courts below vide the impugned judgment and order committed an error of an important question of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice.

5. The plaintiffs of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 filed an application for addition of party and this Court passed the following order dated 3-12-2008 which runs as follows : "Let the application for additional of party be kept with the record."

6. But it appears that the office amended the cause title by inserting the applicant as opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 without any order of this Court.

7. Mr Minhazul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner placed the revisional application, impugned orders, annexures and submits that both the Courts below including the revisional Court without applying their judicial mind and without considering the facts and circumstances and the exceptional circumstances in the case in hand namely, practice of fraud as well as suppression of fact, most illegally and in an arbitrary manner passed the impugned judgments and orders and thereby both Courts below including the revisional Court committed an error of law of an important question of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice. He submits that admittedly, as a general rule, a 3rd party cannot invoke the jurisdiction of this Court but in exceptional circumstances where there is a practice of fraud, intentional suppression or where any right of a party is being highly prejudiced, obviously such party has a right to bring the notice of this Court about such wrong committed by the parties in the proceeding. In support of his contention the learned Advocate referred the decisions reported in 1999 CLC 1526 (Lahore), AIR 1998 (Gujarat) 12 and PLD 1984 SC (AJ & K) 166. He also submits that in the case in hand by excluding certain portion of land from the execution process the Executing Court acted beyond the decree rather the executing Court in the name of exclusion amended the decree passed in other suit, which is not permissible in the eye of law. In support of his contention the learned Advocate also referred the decision reported in 28 DLR (AD) 57. He also submits that it is apparent on the face of the record that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 committed fraud by not mentioning or disclosing the transfer by them in favour of the petitioners though they are made party in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 and, as such, this Court exercising the power conferred under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure can suo muto examine the legality and propriety of the impugned actions.

8. Mr. Oziullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 opposes the Rule. He submits that both the Courts below on proper appreciation of the facts and circumstances and the provision of law has rightly struck down the application of the petitioners on question of maintainability and there is no scope to entertain any application by a 3rd party and, as such, the Courts below committed no error of an important question of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice.

9. It appears that the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 is being added by the office as per the order of this Court dated 3-12-2008. But on perusal of the order sheet it appears that the application of addition of party was neither allowed nor there is any order that the application be considered at the time of hearing of the Rule. It is difficult to understand how the office impleaded the applicants as opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 without any order from this Court, allowing any such addition. In such circumstances, I am unable to allow the learned for the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 to appear before this Court.

10. However, the concerned officers appeared before this Court and prayed for unconditional apology and also assure that they will take utmost care in future regarding nothing down the orders of this Court considering the facts and circumstances and the apology sort by them. I am refrain from taking any disciplinary action against them. However, the concerned officers are directed to be cautious in future.

11. I have perused the impugned judgment and order, judgment and order passed by the trial Court, revisional application, grounds taken thereon, annexures, decisions as referred to and heard the learned Advocates for the contesting parties.

12. On perusal of the same it appears that a partition suit was filed in the year 1958, wherein the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are defendant Nos. 12 and 12(Ka). The suit was decreed on 31-5-1996 and on appeal the same was decreed on compromise on 13-4-1976. In the line of the preliminary decree the final decree was drawn on 28-8-1998 wherein the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 and others got saham. Thereafter, the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 along with others filed Execution Case being Title Execution case No. 2 of 1992 before the Joint District Judge, First Court, Feni. During pendency of the Execution Case the defendants opposite party No. 1 and 2 filed an application before the Execution Court on 9-2-2006 for striking out certain portion of land from the executing process on the ground that they have compromised with the plaintiffs in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005, wherein they were impleaded as defendants. The Execution Court allowed the application. Being aggrieved the petitioner 3rd party filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was rejected and ultimately affirmed by the revisional Court.

<u>13. The first question before this Court that whether an application by 3rd party is maintainable or not in a proceeding as well as in a revisional application before this Court. Since the instant revisional application involved a serious question of law. I am of the view that the instant revisional application is maintainable as per section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure. As a general rule no one can appeal or file a revisional petition from an order unless he is a party to the action or was treated as such or was legal representation of a party or his right in the state or interest is apparent on the face of the record. Admittedly the petitioners are not party in Title Suit No. 157 neither of 1963 nor in Title Appeal No. 170 of 1966 as well as Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1992.</u>

14. But it appears that admittedly the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 who are defendants in the aforesaid suit as well as applicants of the Execution Case transferred the property in question in favour of the petitioner in the years 1996, 1997 and 1998 by registered sale deeds as well as hand over possession. Subsequently, it appears that the added opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 who were wrongly added as opposite party Nos. 3 and 4 in present revisional application filed Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 impleading the present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants, wherein the plaintiffs prayed for a declaration that the judgment and decree passed in the present title suit for partition is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as defendants entered appearance and filed a compromise petition resulting dismissal of the suit. On perusal of the said solenama as well as the judgment and decree passed by that suit it appears that though the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 transferred the land in favour of the petitioners long before filing of the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 but the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 neither disclosed anything the transfer nor mentioned the names of the petitioners in any manner. It appears that in the line of the compromise decree obtained in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 are now trying to strike out certain lands from the executing process. On the facts and circumstances, it appears that the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 suppressed relevant fact in the Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 which not only suppression of fact but also practicing fraud upon the Court of law. In the case of Muhammad Din vs Sher Muhammad reported in 1999 CLC 1'526 (Lahore) the Court held:

"A person if not a party in the trial Court could always prefer an appeal if his rights or interest were adversely affected by a decree likewise he can also revision petition by bringing to the notice of the Court of error about an illegality or material irregularity on the part of the Courts below. This can also be done by the High Court while exercising its suo moat powers in the exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. Therefore a person who was a necessary party and whose rights and interest were adversely affected by a decree and who was not heard is competent to invoke the revisional powers of this Court after establishing his bona fides and the rights and interest that he possesses".

15. In the case of Narayandas Nathumal Hemrajani vs Taraben Kalimuddin Mulla Falchir Society reported in AIR 1998 (Gujarat) 12 it has been held as follows :—

"Now assuming that leave of the Court as per law is required them by subsequent amendment the petitioner has already prayed for leave. As per well recognized principle any amendment made during pendency would relate back to institution unless expressed otherwise. Therefore shall be deemed to have prayed for leave of course the first order expressly does not refer to any leave granted but the fact that petition on behalf of third party is entertained the Court shall be deemed in have granted impliedly as has not been rejected. Therefore, in my view the contention that the petition is without prior leave of the Court is not maintainable. Otherwise also, in my view, looking to section 115 no leave is required if the jurisdiction is invoked by one present before Court but not a party to proceedings. I do not find any express bar to this effect in the said provision. On the contrary under the provisions high Court can suo motu call for record of a subordinate Court and examine the legality of order. Thus the rights conferred under the CP Code unfettered rights and the object is to do substantial justice. The rights can be exercised either suo motu or on being brought to the notice by any party or agency to prevent miscarriage justice. Any party or agency bringing such illegal orders to the notice of Court is merely an instrumentality calling upon the Court to exercise suo motu powers for preventing miscarriage of justice. Therefore in my view under section 115 of the CP Code prior leave of Court is not required when the revision is filed by a person who is person before trial but and yet may not be party".

16. In the case of Khawaja Abdul Kadir vs Abdul Majid reported in PLD 1984 SC (AJ&K) 166 it has been held as follows:-

"So far as point No. (i) listed above is concerned as a general rule no one can appeal or file a revision petition from an order unless he was a party to the action or was treated as such or was a legal representative of a party or his right in the estate or interest are apparent on the face of the record. For that reason the respondent a pro Bono public may not have any interest whatsoever in the cause but that hardly makes any difference. Because we are of the considered view that for exercise of the revisional powers vested in the High Court, there is no bar for anyone to move the High Court to quash the proceedings which were null and void and the High Court on such move is duty bound to take action in proper cases".

<u>17. On perusal of the aforesaid judgments of Indian jurisdiction as well as Pakistan jurisdiction it appears that if a person can show his bona fide right and title apparent on the face of the record as well as can show fraud and suppression of fact can maintain an application in a proceeding even if he is not a party to that Apart from that in the aforesaid decisions it has been observed that this Court even exercising the power conferred under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure can suo muto examine the proceeding when the question of fraud and intentional suppression of fact arise.</u>

18. Admittedly in the case in hand it appears that the present petitioners are bona-fide purchaser of the suit property and they purchased the same long before institution of Title Suit No. 11 of 2005. Not only that they also preferred appeal being Title Appeal No. 19 of 2006 before the appellate Court and the same is pending for adjudication. The present opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 being full aware of the transfer did not disclosed the same in the said suit. Rather compromise the same with the plaintiffs and with the strength of the compromise filed an application for excluding that properties from the instant executing proceeding, as such, I am of the view that the petitioners are not only competent to file the applications but also their applications reserved due consideration in accordance with law.

19. It appears that on the basis of the final decree drawn on 28-8-1990 the parties filed Execution Case being title Execution Case No. 2 of 1992. The law namely the Code of Civil Procedure stipulates the procedures to be followed by the executing Court in execution. It is now a well settled proposition of law is that the executing Court cannot go beyond the decree and it is execute the same in the line of the decree unless and otherwise the same is being altered or modified by any competent Court of law. It appears that in the present Execution Case the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed an application for excluding certain properties on the plea of decree passed in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005. But it appears that the said decree passed in Title Suit No. 11 of 2005 is also challenged by way of appeal being Title Appeal No. 19 of 2006 and the same is now pending for adjudication. Apart from that while such an application is being preferred the Executing Court must apply its judicial mind and considered the same in the spirit of the provision of law namely Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure. In the case of Ramjan Khan alias Ramjan Ali Khan vs Obaidul Huq Chowdhury reported in 28 DLR (AD) 57, their Lordships held as follows :

"It is to be noted that the respondent Obaidul Huq is resisting execution and claiming restoration of possession under rules 100 and 101 of Order XXI of the Code on his own account. It is now well settled that a judgment-debtor under section 47 cannot challenge not can the executing Court go behind the decree to see whether it has been fraudulently obtained. The power of the executing Court to fest the validity of the decree is limited to see whether the decree was passed without jurisdiction or is to nullity or some other exceptional ground as to the executability of the decree. The jurisdiction of the executing Court under Rules 100 and 101 of Order XXI is similarly restricted to the grounds set out above. The same view has been expressed by the Patna High Court in case of Jaisri Lal vs Dulhial, AIR 1930 Patna 416 (The learned Singe Judge acted in excess of his jurisdiction under section 115 CPC in going behind the decree and setting it aside as fraudulent."

20. So it appears that in the aforesaid judgment their Lordships held that the executing Court cannot go behind the decree even on some other exceptional ground as to be executibility of the decree, which is very much apparent in the case in hand.

<u>21. Considering the facts and circumstances provisions of law and the decisions as referred to I am of the view that the revisional Court as well as the executing Court committed an error of an important question of law in rejecting the application of the petitioners which occasioned failure of justice.</u>

22. Accordingly the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The judgments and orders dated 6-3-2008 and 20-2-2006 are herein set aside. The application filed by the petitioners for recalling the order excluding the property from execution is hereby allowed. The further proceeding of Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1992 he stayed till disposal of Title Appeal No. 19 of 2006.

Communicate this order at once.

Office is further decreed to correct the cause Title by deleting name of the opposite party Nos. 3 and 4.

End.

full_judgment:
Md. Abdur Rashid J: This Rule was obtained by defendant No.1 upon making a revision application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and decree dated 25-11-99 passed by the learned Additional District Judge at Bhola in Title Appeal No. 80 of 1997 in reversing those dated 9-6-97 of the Subordinate Judge, First Court at Bhola in Title Suit No.12 of 1992 and in decreeing the suit.

2. The opposite party Nos. 1 to 3 as plaintiffs on 24-3-92 instituted the suit against the petitioner and another for declaration that the 'Sole' (compromise) judgment and decree of the Subordinate Judge at Bhola dated 11-3-92 and 19-3-92 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 is fraudulent, collusive, illegal, null and void, and not binding upon them. The plaint case, in short, is that the entire land of 2.25 acre including the suit land measuring about 1.8925 acre appertaining to RS Khatian No. 604 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 961 was originally possessed by proforma-defendant No. 2, Md Haris as Korsha raiyat under the rent receiver, Usha Rani. Then, Usha Rani obtained a rent decree against Md Haris in Rent Suit No. 2300 of 1955 and in execution of the decree in Rent Execution Case No. 1342 of 1955; the entire land of the Khatian was sold in auction. On 14-1-55 Abdul Barik purchased said 2.25 acre of land in auction and on 17-2-55 he got delivery of possession of said land through Court. While he was thus owner in possession of said 2.25 acre of land, by registered deeds of sale dated 22-7-58 and 8-8-64 Abdul Barik transferred 1.20 acre of land to the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 and delivered them possession. Similarly thereafter, his heirs also transferred the rest of the suit land to the plaintiffs by various registered documents.

3. Thus being owners in possession of the suit land, the plaintiffs encountered with the aforesaid 'Sole' decree, which was fraudulently obtained by the defendant No.1 without making them parties in the suit. Since the decree cast clouds upon their right, title, interest and possession in the suit land, they were constrained to institute the suit.

4. The defendant No. 1 alone appeared and contested the suit by filing a written statement. His main case is that Md Haris transferred the entire land of RS Khatian No. 604 to him by way of pattan by granting a rent receipt. The defendant has since pattan been in possession of the entire land of the Khatian. He also denied the possession of Abdul Barik as well as of the plaintiff in the suit land.

5. On the pleadings, various issues, namely, whether the suit as framed is maintainable; whether the suit is barred by limitation; whether the plaintiffs got any right, title or possession in the suit land and whether the impugned decree is binding upon the plaintiffs were framed.

6. In support of their case, the plaintiffs examined three witnesses and adduced their title documents, which were marked as exhibit 1 series and the defendant also examined 3 witnesses and adduced a counterfoil of a rent receipt, an 'Angiranama' and an information slip, which were marked as exhibit Nos. 'Ka', 'Kha' and 'Ga.'

7. The trial Court dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case of auction purchase of the suit land by Abdul Barik and that the plaintiffs acquired no title in the suit land. On appeal therefrom at the instance of the plaintiffs, the appellate Court on consideration of the evidence on record allowed the appeal, set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit as prayed for.

8. Mr M Shamsul Alam, learned Counsel for the petitioner, at the outset assailed the instant suit on the ground of maintainability. He submits that the suit as framed in impugning the 'Sole' decree dated 11-3-92 passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 is not maintainable in the absence of seeking further declaration of title in the suit land. In support, he cites the decisions in the case of Md Yunus vs Md Yusuf, 21 DLR 466; Imanuddin Rarhi vs Lilabati Das, 32 DLR 75; MA Mallik vs MH Mallik, 6 BCR (AD) 56 and Sufia Khanom vs Faizunnessa, 39 DLR (AD) 46. He next submits that the Court of appeal below erred in law in finding the title of the plaintiffs in the suit land on the basis of copies of sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession, which were never admitted into the evidence in accordance with law. Moreover, he draws our attention to the documents and submits that the documents appear to be fabricated and created for the suit. Lastly, he submits that the finding of the appellate Court on possession will not be binding in revision in that the finding is based on those inadmissible sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession and arrived at, in the absence of any proof, that Abdul Barik ever got possession of the suit land.

9. Opposing the Rule, Dr Rafiqur Rahman, learned Senior Counsel, on the other hand, submits that the plaintiffs have convincingly proved to be in possession of the suit land for more than the statutory period of limitation on assertion of their right, title and interest and they are therefore, entitled to challenge and have the fraudulent 'Sole' decree, obtained by defendant No.1 behind their back in respect of their land, declared null and void and not binding upon them. In such suit, according to him, the plaintiffs are not required to seek further decree for declaration of their title in the suit land. In support of his submission, he cites the decision in the case of Abdus Sukur vs Bhasan Mondal, 1 BLC 549.

10. Dr Rafiqur Rahman was however, very candid in not relying upon the questioned sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession to defend the impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below. He submits that if the plaintiffs can prove their possession in the suit land for more than the statutory period of limitation without any reference to those papers of even on imperfect documents, they can maintain the suit and defend the decree. Lastly, he submits that the trial Court did not at all consider the issue on possession, which was the moot issue in the suit and the appellate Court below, on due consideration of the depositions of both PWs and DWs examined by parties in the light of the documentary evidence on record, has found the plaintiffs in possession of the suit land and such finding has become concluded by the decision of the final Court of facts. This finding on possession, therefore, cannot be disturbed in revision.

11. We have perused the record. Admitted position is that the entire land measuring 2.25 acre appertaining to RS Khatian No. 604 was correctly recorded in the name of proforma defendant No. 2, Md Haris as a Korsha raiyot under Usha Rani. Usha Rani obtained a rent decree against said Haris in the Rent Suit No. 2300 of 1955 and in execution of the decree got the tenancy sold in auction in Rent Execution case No.1342 of 1955. Case of the plaintiffs is that Abdul Barik purchased the entire land in said auction sale and on 17-2-55 got delivery of possession through Court. While the defendant No.1 though admitted such auction sale but took the stand that Abdul Batik could not take delivery of possession and, as such, the auction was not acted upon.

<u>12. In the trial Court, the plaintiffs got exemption from filing the writ of delivery of possession. A copy of the sale certificate was though filed in Court but the plaintiffs ultimately did not tender the same for admission into evidence. The plaintiffs however, adduced number of registered sale deeds evidencing their purchase and possession of the suit land from said Abdul Barik and others from 22-7-58 up to 28-6-87, which were marked exhibits as 1 series. The trial Court however, has not said anything about the genuineness or otherwise of said title documents. As stated above, the plaintiffs examined three witnesses while defendant No.1 also examined equal number of witnesses in the suit. The appellate Court appears to have relied upon said sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession, which was for the first time filed in appeal. We could not find any order admitting the sale certificate and writ of delivery of possession as additional evidence and marking them as exhibits. In the circumstances, we do not have any hesitation to say that the Court of appeal below was wrong to rely upon the sale certificate and the writ of delivery of possession in proof of auction sale and delivery of possession as well.</u>

13. The moot issue we are facing is, whether the impugned judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below in declaring the compromise decree dated 11-3-92 passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 illegal and void can be sustained in law.

14. We have closely examined the finding of the Court of appeal on the issue of possession. We find that the appellate Court on consideration of the depositions of all the PWs and DWs has come to the finding that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land, and the defendant No.1 has got no possession. We find such conclusion on possession is well borne out by the evidence on record. Nothing could be suggested from the side of the petitioner that such finding be based on misreading or non-reading of any material evidence on record. If it is so, the plaintiffs must be held to have entered into possession of 0.40 acre on 22-7-58 and 0.80 acre of the suit land on 8-8-64. So, their possession in such land spread over more than the statutory period of 12 years is sufficient to perfect their title. Even if they fail to prove their predecessor-in-interest, Abdul Barik got delivery of possession in the suit land through Court by producing and proving a writ of delivery of possession, they are yet entitled to challenge the decree obtained in respect of their land by the defendant No.1 behind their back for the simple reason that if such decree is left outstanding that clouds and affects their right, interest and/or possession in the suit land. The failure of the plaintiffs to prove the entry of Abdul Barik by proving a writ of delivery of possession also loses all its importance after the admission of the auction sale by defendant No.1 in paragraph 14 of his written statement.

15. Be that as it may, now we shall see how far the decision of the Court of appeal below that the 'Sole' (compromise) decree dated 11-3-92 obtained by the defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 is illegal, collusive and hence, void is correct. In coming to such decision, the Court of appeal below first found that the persons who are in possession of the land covered and affected by such decree were not made parties in the suit, and the decree was deliberately obtained behind their back. Secondly, defendant No.1 failed to prove his any leasehold interest or possession in the suit land.

16. We have already affirmed the finding of the Court of appeal below that the plaintiffs have proved their long possession in the suit land on the basis of their purchase vide exhibits 1 series, and defendant No. 1 failed to prove his possession in any part of the suit land. On 6-7-91 defendant No.1 instituted Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 against proforma defendant No. 2, Md Haris only for declaration of his title in the entire land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 604 including the suit land by way of a lease. Said RS Khatian appears to have recorded the name of Md Haris as Korsha raiyat under the rent receiver, Usha Rani. According to the list of rent receivers of the area at the relevant time as printed at page 14 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by the Dhaka Law Reports, Second Edition, such Korsha raiyot had no rent receiving interest. If it is so, such Korsha raiyot had no right under law to create any sub-tenancy in respect of said land. The case of the defendant No.1 that he took lease of the suit land from proforma defendant No. 2, therefore, falls through as a hoax. Neither in this suit nor in the earlier suit, he could say definitely when he actually took lease. He just produced a piece of paper dated 5-1-55 to evidence an admission of proforma defendant No. 2 as to lease, which he did not take any step to prove. Dr Rafiqur Rahman has submitted that in 1955 no one could validly lease out any land. It may also be mentioned that the defendant No. 1 did not say a word about such admission of proforma defendant No. 2 in his earlier suit. Similarly, he got marked exhibit 'Kha' which appears to be a counterfoil of a rent receipt, which was also not proved.

17. Besides, proforma defendant No. 2, Md Haris did not turn up either to contest the claim of the plaintiffs or support the case of the defendant No.1 though the suit was brought within a week of the compromise decree signed.

<u>18. We have considered the case of lease of defendant No. 1 so detailed in order to be convinced that the relief for declaration of title on the basis of lease as sought for by defendant No.1 in the earlier suit has got no basis whatsoever. Without impleading necessary persons who are in possession of the land and without having any semblance of right, title, interest and/or possession in the land of the suit jote, defendant No. 1 fraudulently obtained the decree in the earlier suit upon false claims.</u>

<u>19. In the circumstances, we do not find any reason to take a view different from that of the Court of appeal below that the comprise decree obtained by defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 is illegal and void.</u>

<u>20. Lastly, we must answer the technical submission of Mr Shamsul Alam on the maintainability of the suit. The issue on maintainability as framed in the suit was answered by the trial Court in the affirmative in favour of the plaintiffs. Against the finding, no objection was however raised by the defendant No. 1 in the appeal. Now, Mr Shamsul Alam submits, for the first time, that the instant suit for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in aforesaid Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 in the absence of further relief, namely, further declaration of title of the plaintiffs in the suit land is not maintainable. We have closely scrutinised the decisions cited by both sides. In the cases of Md Yunus vs Md Yusuf and Imanuddin Rarhi vs Lilabati Das, declaration was sought against benami transaction. They are of no help. One of us sitting single wrote the opinion in the case of Abdus Sukur vs Bhasani Mondal. In the case, all the decisions on the point including those of the Appellate Division in the cases of MA Mallik vs MH Mallik and Sufia Khanam vs Faizunnessa were considered. In quite agreement, we endorse the view expressed in the decision that if a person in possession of a land on assertion of his right, title and interest finds a decree obtained by any other person in respect of such land affecting his interest or possession, or clouding his right or title in such land, he is always entitled to have such decree adjudged or declared void. Such suit will be governed by section 39 not by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. When such person is not a party to such decree, he does need to get the decree set aside or cancelled. Under such law, he is also not required to seek further declaration that the decree is not binding upon him or that he has got title in the suit land.</u>

21. In the above view of the matter that we have taken, we find the ultimate decision of the Court of appeal below declaring the judgment and decree of the Subordinate Judge at Bhola in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 dated 11-3-92 illegal, collusive and hence, void is quite correct and does not call for any interference. And such decision has not resulted in any failure of justice.

22. In the result, the Rule is discharged without, however, any order as to costs. Order of stay as granted at the time of issue of the Rule is hereby recalled and vacated. The impugned judgment and decree reversing those of the trial Court in declaring the judgment and decree dated 11-3-92 and 19-3-92 respectively of the Subordinate Judge at Bhola in Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 void are hereby affirmed.

Send down the records at once.

End.

lawyer:
Md Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan with Sikder Mahmudur Razi, Advocates—For the Appellant. 
Hafizur Rahman and Md Boktiar Hossain, Advocates—For the Respondents.
parties:
Bangladesh Karma Sangsthan Sangstha ------ Plaintiff-Appellant
vs
Power Development Board and others ------ Defendant Respondents.
full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J: This appeal is directed at the instance of the plaintiff-appellant against the judgment and decree dated 24-11-1991 and decree signed on 1-12-1991 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 159 of 1987 in dismissing the suit.

2. The appellant as plaintiffs instituted an Other Class Suit No. 159 of 1987 for a declaration that the defendant is legally bound to sup-ply the articles as per the supply and delivery order contained in Memo No. DCT G/37225/ 1808 dated 5-5-87 to the plaintiff and to declare the Memo No. D-Chittagong/3-225/2041 dated 8-6-87 issued under the signature of the defendant No. 3 is illegal, harassing and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff and further to declare that the defendants are bound to issue work order for the supply of 'kha' schedule articles as per Memo No. DCT G/3-225/11721 dated 23-4-87 to the plaintiff and also to declare that the acceptance of tender on 26-10-87 on the basis of auction notice dated 10-10-87 is illegal, without jurisdiction, and motivated and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff. The plaintiffs further prayer is to pass an order of injunction restraining the defendants from supplying the goods to anyone other than the plaintiff.

3. That the facts of the plaint is that the plaintiff being a social welfare organization filed an application on 24-9-84 to the Minister for Energy and Mineral Resources expressing his desire to purchase the old and unusable goods of Power Development. Board at the reserve price of the Board, the application was recommended and forwarded to the defendant No. 2 Mr Shafiul Azam the Minister for Power and Energy Ministry and the said application was also recommended by Major General Shamsul Haque the Minster for Health and Family Welfare. The defendant No. 2 prepared a survey report regarding the old goods and on the basis of the survey report the defendants decided to sell the old unusable goods.  Thereafter the defendant No. 3 sent a letter to the plaintiff organization on 23-4-1987 vide Memo No. DCTG /3-225-172 informing the plaintiff that the defendants are ready to sell some old un-useable goods to the plaintiff at the Deserve price of the Board. In that letter it was mentioned that if the plaintiff is ready to purchase those old and un-useable goods they will have to communicate their decision to the defendants within 5 days. That after receiving the letter, the plaintiff organization on 26-4-87 informed the defendant No. 3 that they are ready to purchase the goods/articles of 'ka' and 'Kha' schedules. Thereafter on 3-5-87 the defendant No. 3 issued an work order to sell the articles of 'Ka' schedule to the plaintiff vide Memo No. DCT G/3-225/1408 and fixed the price of 'ka' schedule articles at Taka 1,71,478 and asked the plaintiff to deposit the said amount to the account No. STD-3 of the Sonali Bank Hathazari Branch, Chittagong.

4. The plaintiff organization, within the said time deposited Taka 1,71,478 to the account mentioned earlier and informed the defendants. Thereafter, the defendant No.3 by his Memo No DCT G/3-225/1808 dated 5-5-87 acknowledged the payment made by the plaintiff and requested the plaintiff to take delivery of the goods of 'ka' schedule within 20 days. The defendants gave issue vouchers to the plaintiff organization. In this way defendant sold 'ka' schedule articles/goods to the plaintiff and the plaintiff became owner of the articles of 'ka' schedule.

5. Thereafter, on 16-5-87 when the plaintiff organization went to the defendant No. 9-10 to take delivery of articles/goods they refused to give delivery of the goods to the plaintiff and informed the plaintiff organization that the higher authority has given instruction not to delivery the goods to the plaintiff. That being failed to receive delivery of the articles/goods on 19-5-87 the plaintiff wrote a letter to the defendant No. 3 intimating the incident, but he did not give any reply. Thereafter on 8-6-87 the defendant No. 3 vide Memo No. D-Chittagong/ 3-335/2041 cancelled the work order and delivery order issued in favour of the plaintiff and by this letter asked the plaintiff to take back the money deposited by him. That on 20-6-87 the plaintiff organization again gave a letter to the defendant No. 3 and requested him to deliver the articles/goods to the plaintiff and the copy of the letter was also forwarded to the defendant Nos. 4-6, but the defendants did not pay any heed to it. That on 10-10-87 the defendant No. 3 published an auction notice in the 'Daily Purba Kone' on behalf of the defendant No. 1 inviting tender for the sale of the aforesaid goods. That the plaintiff organization on 12-10-87 sent a legal notice to the defendants through its lawyer asking them to withdraw the auction notice and to deliver the articles/goods of 'ka' schedule to the plaintiff. Without giving any reply of the legal notice, the defendants fixed 19-10-87 for accepting the tender. That for the reason of general strike called by the Opposition throughout the country, on that day tender could not be dropped by any one. Thereafter, the defendant without giving any further auction notice, on 26-10-87 most illegally has accepted the tender from some persons. The defendants at any time may deliver the articles/goods to any one they chose. The plaintiff has filed this suit for declaration and for permanent injunction so that the articles/good of 'ka' schedule cannot be delivered to any one other than the plaintiff.

6. The defendant-respondent contested the suit by filing written statements denying all the material allegations made in the plaintiff contending inter alia that the plaintiff organization is a fake one. Although it has been shown that the organization is a registered organization, in fact there is no registration of the said organization. These is no any organization namely বাংলাদেশ কর্মসংস্থান সংস্থা given by the plaintiff. The person who signed the plaint as secretary of the organization is not the secretary; there is no any organization in the name of বাংলাদেশ  কর্মসংস্থান সংস্থা Tongi Shere Bangla Market, once there was an organization which has been closed for anti organizational activity of the then secretary Abdul Hannan. There is no any power of attorney in favour of Mr AKM Abdul Haque as the secretary of the organization, Mr AKM Abdul Haque is a man of Feni. He is a fake businessman lives in Chittagong and he runs his business with false identity. He used to manage recommendation from the Ministers and obtain work order and in this way he has been misappropriating money. Since the work order has been obtained by committing fraud and it has been given in violation of the existing rules, the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief and the orders obtained by the plaintiff are void. The plaintiff organization fraudulently has obtained the recommendation of the ministers to obtain the work order and delivery order of unusable articles/goods of Power Development Board mentioned in schedule 'ka'. The plaintiff obtained work order for the goods of 'Ka' schedule. They did not have any work order of the goods of 'kha' schedule. That after giving the work order on 5-5-87 the defendants could realize that the orders have been given in violation of the store manual; as per provision of the store manual there is a provision for inviting tenders through advertisement in the newspaper and the highest bidder is entitled to get the work order, since this provision of law has been ignored, the work order and the delivery order has been cancelled. Since the work order and the delivery order have been obtained fraudulently by the plaintiff organization, the defendants had no other option but to cancel those two orders. The defendants requested the plaintiff organization to take back their money. The plaintiff in no way has the right to get the delivery of the 'ka' schedule goods. The defendant fixed 18-10-87 to sell the unusable goods/articles by auction fixing 19-10-87 for dropping tender which was extended till 26-1-87 and 20 persons participated in auction of the goods/articles of 'ka' and 'kha' schedule and out of 20 bidders Taher Brothers and Modern Electric Enterprise became successful and their bid was at Taka 5,21,010 and 3,79,000 respectively and these two bidders were given the work order. If the plaintiff organization would have given the delivery of the goods/articles the defendant Power Development Board would have to incur loss of Taka 6/7 lacs, the defendant had no any bad intention but to protect the interest of the Power Development Board they have done everything fairly with good faith and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed.

7. In the context of the pleadings the trial Court framed as many as 7 issues. The plaintiff side adduced 2 witnesses and the defendant examined only one witness as DW 1. After considering the facts and circumstance pleadings of the parties, evidences and other materials on the record the trial Court dismissed the suit mainly on the ground that the work order and delivery order of the goods/articles of 'ka' schedule was given in favour of the plaintiff in violation of the store manual of Power Development Board. That being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong the plaintiff has preferred this appeal.

8. Mr Md Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan appeared with Mr Sikder Mahmudur Razi the learned Advocate on behalf of the appellate submits that the plaintiff organization is a registered organization and they have obtained many work orders for the organization previously, in this regard he referred Exhibit 13 series those are the letters between the plaintiff organization and other organizations including the defendant No. 3 which shows the plaintiff organization has a legal entity at the time of obtaining work order from the defendant side.

9. Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan the learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that বাংলাদেশ কর্মসংস্থান সংস্থা had its office at Shere Bangla Market which was shifted to 7 Morkum (Tissue gate) Gazipur on 1-12-87. In this regard Mr Bakir refers Exhibit 14 the certificate issued by the Chairman Tongi Pourashava; the contents of the certificate reads as  follows:

বাংলাদেশ কর্মসংস্থান সংস্থা টংগী থানা কার্যানির্বাহী পরিষদ কার্যালয়টি (চেরাগ আলীস্থ) শেরে বাংলা মার্কেট হইতে ১-১২-৮৭ইং তারিখে ৭নং মরকুম (টিসু গেইটে) টংগী, গাজীপুর ঠিকানায় স্থানান্তর করা হইয়াছে।

Mr Bakir also refers another certificate given by the Social Welfare officer, Ramna, Paltan, Dhaka the contents of the said certificate runs as follows:

বাংলাদেশ কর্মসংস্থান সংস্থা টংগী থানা কার্যানির্বাহী পরিষদ দেশের বৃহত্তর স্বার্থে বিভিন্ন প্রকল্প চালাইয়া আসিতেছে। তাহাদের সমাজ সেবামূলক কার্যাক্রম অত্যন্ত সন্তোষজনক, ইহা একটি বৈধ নিবন্ধিকরণ সংস্থা।

10. This certificate has been marked as Exhibit 15. Mr Bakir further submits that upon an application from the plaintiff the defendants prepared a survey report and asked the plaintiff whether they are ready to take the goods as per the survey report. The plaintiff expressed his desire to purchase the goods of "ka" and "kha" schedule and being fully satisfied the defendant No. 3 accepted the offer and agreed to sell the articles/goods and accordingly the defendant asked the plaintiff to deposit the money and to take the delivery of goods. The plaintiff deposited money to the account of the defendants and the plaintiff also got delivery order but when the plaintiff went to receive the goods the defendant side refused to deliver the articles/goods. It is a clear violation of the provision of contract and also violation of the principle of natural justice.

11. In this regard Mr Bakir referring some exhibits further submits that the Exhibit 2 is a letter given by the defendant No.3 to the plaintiff organization asking them to let the defendant know whether the plaintiff is ready to purchase the unusable goods of the Power Development Board within 5 days. Exhibit 3 is the consent of the plaintiff organization to purchase the goods/articles and the Exhibit 4 is an work order issued by the defendant No. 3 in favour of the plaintiff. Exhibit 5 is the delivery order and the Exhibit 6 are issue vouchers from the defendant's side. From the above documents it appears that the defendants accepting proposal had issued work order and delivery order in favour of the plaintiff. Exhibit 7 is a letter given by the plaintiff to the defendant No. 3 mentioning that they went to take delivery of the articles to the store, but the store keeper refused to given delivery of the articles/goods without assigning any reason. Exhibit 8 is a letter given by the defendant No. 3 by which respondent No. 3 has asked the store keepers to stop delivery of the goods. Exhibit 9 is a letter given by the defendant respondent No. 3 informing the plaintiff that the work order and delivery order earlier given to them is cancelled. Ext 10 is a letter of the plaintiff to the defendant No.3 requesting him to deliver the goods in his favour. Exhibit 11 is the auction notice published in the "Daily Purbokon" inviting fresh tender Exhibit 12 is a notice given by the lawyer of the plaintiff to the defendant requesting him to deliver the goods in favour of the plaintiff.

12. Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan further submits that there was offer and acceptance for selling 'ka' schedule property and to give effect of the contract, the work order and delivery order was made and in pursuance of that the plaintiff deposited entire money and the plaintiff was directed to take delivery of goods; at this stage defendant cannot get out of the contract on the plea that the contract was done in violation of the Store Manual, because when the work order and delivery order was made at that time the Store Manual was there, the defendant gave consent to sale the goods on the basis of an application filed by the plaintiff which was duly recommended by the high officials of the Power Development Board and also by the concerned Minister. In this regard he drew the attention of this Court to the deposition of the DW 1 the defendant No. 3 in this cross examination he stated that- বাদীর দরখাস্ত এ তদানিন্তন দুই জন মন্ত্রী একজন শফিউল আজম অপরজন মেজর জেনারেল শামসুল হক মাল সরবরাহের জন্য সুপারিশ করিয়াছিলেন। This defendant also stated in his cross-examination that, দুই মন্ত্রী রিকমান্ডেশন এর ব্যাপারে কোন তদন্ত করি নাই। যেহেতু উক্ত দরখাস্ত কর্তৃপক্ষের মাধ্যমে আমাদের অফিসে আসে। দুইজন মন্ত্রীর রিকমান্ডেশন এবং আমাদের চেয়ারম্যান চিফ ইঞ্জিনিয়ার, সুপারিনটেডেন্ট ইঞ্জিনিয়ার তাহাদের নির্দেশ যায়। সম্পূর্ণরুপে সন্তুষ্ট হইয়া বিরোধীয় ক তপশিলের মালামাল বাদীর নিকট বিক্রয়ের প্রস্তাব করি।

13. Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan submits that the defendants being fully satisfied had accepted the proposal of the plaintiff and agreed to sell the goods to the plaintiff, accordingly they issued work order to the plaintiff, asked them to deposit money and issued the delivery order and at this stage the defendant cannot retreat from the contract on the plea that the work order and delivery order was issued in violation of the Store Manual, in this regard. Mr Mohammad Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan refers the case of Jammu and Kashmir vs Sanna Ullah Mir reported in AIR 1966 Jammu and Kashmir page 45. In this case it has been held that ignorance is no ground of way of contract. It is well settled that ignorance of law is no excuse and a party cannot be allowed to get any relief on the ground that it had done a particular and in ignorance of the state of the law. Section 21 of the Contract Act, which lays down that a contract cannot be avoided even if it was caused by a mistake of law gives statutory recognition to this doctrine." Mr Bakir submits as his last submission that since contract has been completed the defendants cannot retract from their own commitment and refuse to deliver the suit articles goods on the ground that the contract was done by mistake of law.

14. Mr Hafizur Rahman the learned Advocate on behalf of Mr Md Boktiar Hossain appears on behalf of the defendant submits that since contract was done in violation of the Store Manual the authority has rightly cancelled the work order and delivery order, in this regard he refers the Exhibit 'Kha' the Store Manual of the Power Development Board particularly rule 22 of the said manual in which there is a provision to sell the goods by auction publishing the auction notice in the national dailies and the sale will normally be made to the highest bidders with due regard to the reserve value/market value of the scrap as far as practicable. In this case the provision has not been followed by the defendants, later on when the defendants realized that they have issued the work order and delivery order in violation of the Store Manual they have cancelled the work order and delivery order immediately. Learned Advocate further submits that when the wrong is detected it should not be allowed to be continued, when the defendant could realize their wrong doing they immediately stopped the supply order and the delivery order. Mr Hafizur Rahman further submits that the plaintiff must succeed his case on the merit of his own case he cannot succeed the case on the weakness of defendants the Court below has rightly dismissed the suit of the plaintiff. In this regard he refers the case of Md Naimuddin Sarder vs Md Abdul Kalam Biswas 39 DLR (AD) 237.

15. The short fact of the case of the appellant is that the appellant-plaintiff applied to the defendants to purchase some unusable old articles from the stores of Power Development Board at reserve price. The defendants agreed to sell some goods/articles to the plaintiff and accordingly the defendant issued work order and delivery order after receiving money. When the plaintiff-appellant went to the delivery station, the defendant refused to deliver the goods and the respondent defendants can-celled the order without assigning any reason. Later on the respondent defendant gave a letter of cancellation of delivery order.

16. The respondent defendant entered into a contract to sell old goods of Power Development Board, the contract was completed the plaintiff organization deposited money for the goods and he was asked to take delivery of the goods from the store the defendant can-not retract from their own commitment.

17. The defendant's case is that the delivery order was made in violation of the provision of Store Manual thus the order was cancelled. There is no any scope to delivery the goods in violation of the provision of law. It is to be mentioned here that the defendant agreed to sell only 'ka' schedule goods although the plaintiff wanted to purchase 'ka' and 'kha' schedule goods/articles.

18. We have gone through the record, the exhibits and the evidence adduced by the witnesses. It appears that the PW-1 Mrs Delwara Begum adduced evidence on behalf of the plaintiff organization being an attorney. She stated that on 5-5-87 the defendants asked the plaintiff to take delivery of goods vide Exhibit 5 and on 21-5-87 the defendants stopped delivery of goods and informed the plaintiffs vide Exhibit 8. In her cross examination she stated that the plaintiff organization is not a fake organization, the defendants several times delivered goods to the plaintiff. In this regard she exhibited number of letters which were marked as Exhibit 13 series. In support of the genuineness of the plaintiff organization she referred Exhibit 13 and 15, the certificates issued by the Tongi Pourashava and the Social Welfare office. She categorically denied the suggestion that the plaintiff organization is fake one. The PW 2 had supported the plaintiffs' case. DW 1 the Executive Engineer (defendant No.3) in his cross examination stated that the application of the plaintiff was recommended by the two Ministers, he has also stated that the plaintiff deposited Taka 1,71,478 for 'ka' schedule goods/articles and the defendant accepted it for 'ka' schedule articles and gave delivery order in favour of the plaintiffs. He further stated that the proposal of the plaintiff was accepted and work order and delivery order was given accordingly. He further stated that regarding recommendation by the two ministers they did not hold any inquiry the application of the plaintiff came through proper channel. The application was recommended by two ministers and the Chairman, Chief Engineer of the Board and Superintending Engineer gave order to issue work order and delivery order to sell articles of 'ka' schedule to the plaintiff. He further stated that being fully satisfied they issued the work order in favour of the plaintiff. He further stated that the defendants have delivered goods to the plaintiff organization earlier also. He further stated in his cross examination that it was not mentioned that the plaintiff organization is a fake one in the letter dated 8-6-87 Exhibit 7. He also stated that in that letter nothing was mentioned regarding store manual. He expressed his ignorance regarding the existence of the plaintiffs organization, he also stated that he does not know whether the plaintiff organization is unregistered or registered. He also stated that the defendants have not lodged any complaint regarding the plaintiffs organization to the Anti-Corruption or to any Court. He further stated in his cross examination that it is not clearly written in the Store Manual that tender notice is to be given in the Daily Newspaper for the sale of the old goods. He further stated that if the plaintiffs Tongi office is found to be genuine they are bound to supply the goods to the plaintiff.

<u>19. We have gone through the materials on record, it appears to us that there was a contract between the parties. As per contract the plaintiff deposited to the defendant's bank and the defendant being fully satisfied has given the work order and delivery order of the goods in favour of the plaintiff. The defendant suddenly wanted to retract from his commitment saying that the work order and delivery order has been given in violation of the Store Manual. The reason for retraction from the contract by the defendant was not assigned to the plaintiff which defeats the principle of natural justice. It is admitted by the defendant that on the recommendation of the two ministers and high officials of the Power Development Board the work order and delivery order was given. From the deposition of DW 1 it is clear that being fully satisfied the defendants issued work order and delivery order to the plaintiff, at this stage it cannot be said that the orders were issued by mistake of law. The defendants cannot get rid of the contract.</u>

<u>20. In this regard the decision cited by Mr Bakir Uddin Bhuiyan learned advocate for the appellant is pertinent, which says that either of the parties cannot retreat from the contract even if the contract has been done by mistake of law. The learned trial Court has failed to appreciate that the defendants without assigning any reason arbitrarily has cancelled the work order and delivery order. The reason for cancelling the orders was not mentioned anywhere, subsequently they said that the contract was entered into in violation for the Store Manual of the Board which does not exonerate the defendants from performing the obligations. The work order and delivery order was issued after depositing money by the plaintiff as per survey report prepared by the defendants. The learned trial Court should have considered this aspect of the case. Citation given by the learned Advocate for the defendant has got very little applicability in this case. In this decision it has been held that the plaintiff in order to succeed must establish his own case to obtain a decree and weakness of defendants case is no ground for passing a decree in favour of the plaintiff. We are of the view that the plaintiff has been succeeded to prove his case. The Store Manual, particularly the rule 22 of the manual is a guide line, its deviation might be an irregularity but the contract which has been entered into with the knowledge of the concerned minister and all other higher officials of the Board cannot be said illegal for deviation from the guideline. The Court below has failed to appreciate this aspect of the case, with the above we are of the view that the judgment and decree passed by the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong On 24-11-1981 is not proper and we are inclined to interfere with the same and accordingly the same is set aside. The order of cancellation of delivery order dated 8-6-1987 contained in Memo No. Chittagong-/3-225 /2041 is cancelled and the delivery order dated 5-5-1987 vide Memo No. DCTG/3-225 /1808 is hereby restored. The respondents are directed to deliver the 'ka' schedule goods to the appellant-plaintiff as per Memo dated 5-5-1987 within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.</u>

21. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.

Send down the lower Court record at once.

End.
