parties:
Swadhin Chandra Mandal and others ------Petitioners
vs
Bangladesh University Grants Commission (UGC) and others ------Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Khurshid Alam Sarkar J: This Rule has been calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the impugned Memo No. UGC/Admin/paboishwa/402(Tadanto)/08/8 200 dated 25-10-2011, issued under the signature of Respondent No. 6 being directed by Respondents No. 1 and 4, suspending the admission of students in BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) Course of the Patuakhali Science and Technology University in the session of 2011 and thereby staying the Memo No. (UGC/Admin/paboishwa/402 (Tadanto)/ 08/8200 dated 29-9-2011 should not be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

2. Facts leading to the issuance of this Rule, in short, are that Petitioner No. 1 is a guardian of a prospective student (Application PIN No. 565296 and Roll No. 10346) who sought admission in the BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) Degree Course under Unit-A of the Patuakhali Science Technology University (hereinafter referred to as PSTU and was qualified in the admission test held on 10-12-2011, the result of which was published on the same day. Petitioner No. 2 is a student who sat in the said admission test as stated above under the said Unit-A (Application PIN No. 894391 and Roll No. 10146) and he has been kept in the waiting list and, currently, waiting for admission in the department of Animal Husbandry (Hons) Degree Course of PSTU. Petitioner No. 3 is the Joint Secretary of Bangladesh Animal Husbandry Association (Herein-after referred to as AHA) and, currently, acting General Secretary of the said Association, who has been fighting long for opening up the BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) Degree course in the different Universities throughout the country for expansion of education in the field of animal production with a comprehensive curriculum for the said Hons Degree course. It is alleged in the writ petition that with the advancement of the society when the demand of higher education in Animal Husbandry course is being pressed by the citizens of the country, particularly the people working in production of animals, in the context of the increasing demands of the qualified persons in that field and, at this juncture, the Bangladesh Veterinary Association (hereinafter referred to as BVA) all along resisted opening up the said course throughout the country and accordingly on 25-4-2011 the said BVA made representation to the University Grants Commission (hereinafter referred to as UGC) not to open any such course of Animal Husbandry (Hons) Degree Course in PSTU whereupon the Ministry of Education on 6-6-2011 directed the Respondent No. 3 for taking necessary action. As such, the said Ministry on 17-7-2011 directed the concerned authority not to open the BSc Animal Husbandry (Hons) Degree Course throughout the country. Thereafter, several representations were made by the Bangladesh Animal Husbandry Association and also by Babugonj Shikkha & Samajik Unnayan Bastobayon Parishad, a local social welfare organization, on 21-8-2011 addressing the Hon'ble Minister for Ministry of Education, who, on the same day upon consideration of the representation and having been satisfied, recommended for opening up the said course in the PSTU. Subsequently, the Ministry vide their letter dated 25-8-2011 withdrew their previous letter dated 6-6-2011 and directed the UGC to give their opinion upon scrutinizing the matter. Thereafter, on 20-9-2011 the Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee for Education and on 25-9-2011 the local MP issued 2(two) DO letters consecutively to do the needful for opening up the said course. Then, the UGC on 26-9-2011 gave their opinion in favour of opening up the new Department and on 29-9-2011 the UGC gave its nod to open up the said course for, the session 2011-12 and pursuant to the said approval the PSTU published amended admission notification on 2-10-2011 fixing 10-12-2011 for admission test and 22-12-2011 for Admission. After publication of the aforesaid notification for admission by PSTU, the BVA made further representation to the UGC, who, by convening a meeting on 20-10-2011, resolved to circulate a press release announcing that a 7 member sub-committee was to be formed which was to submit a report within 7 days and till submission of their report admission in Animal Husbandry (Hons) Course would be suspended and, accordingly, on 25-10-2011 the UGC suspended the admission of the said course and withdrew their 'earlier approval letter. On 20-10-2011 4(four) members, including the Dean, who attended the aforesaid meeting made representation to the UGC stating that the meeting was held to take arbitrary decision to abolish the Animal Husbandry education and profession. It is stated that though the UGC was supposed to form a 7 member committee which was to submit their report within 7(seven) days from 20-10-2011 but the said 7 member committee was formed lately vide office order dated 25-10-2011 and till dated no report has been submitted and even not a single meeting was convened by the said committee. Since this particular BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) course was included under Unit-A despite suspension order of UGC by the impugned memo, the PSTU had no other alternative but to complete the admission process of the students under Unit-A to save the lives of the prospective students and thereafter, the PSTU completed the admission test of Unit-A on 10-12-2011 and result of Unit-A was published on 10-12-2011 but due to suspension order regarding admission of BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) Course, the petitioners and other qualified students (30 students) could not get admitted in the said post. Thereafter, several representations were made by AHA (the petitioners Association) but without any result though according to the admission circular the last date of admission from merit test was fixed on 19-12-2011 and on 20-12-2011 but the respondents had not paid any heed to sort out the petitioners grievance. Finding no other alternative, the petitioners No. 1, 2 and 3 approached this Court and obtained Rule with an order of stay. After issuance of the Rule and order of stay, the PSTU on 15-1-2012 caused special admission notification fixing 25-1-2012 for reporting and 26-1-2012 for admission. On 26-1-2012 by 4-00 PM out of 110 students 30 students were allowed and they were admitted in the said course on their applications.

3. The Rule was contested by the UGC (respondent Nos. 1, 4 and 6) and the BVA, the added respondents No. 8 and 9, who have opposed the Rule by filing separate sets of affidavits-in-opposition. In the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the UGC it is contended that the facts stated in the writ petition are not correct and the petitioners have no locus-standi to file this writ petition and they do not have any grievance to file the instant writ petition. It is stated that the initial approval was accorded by the UGC relying on the wrong information supplied by the PSTU. It is further stated that the duration of the course of such Hons degree created the whole problem and in its affidavit the UGC blamed the PSTU for all the anomalies. It is further stated that the PSTU is solely responsible for creating this anomalous situation as it acted malafide to harass the government as well as the other respondents. It is alleged in the affidavit-in-opposition that even after suspension order issued by the UGC with a direction to stop admission is the said program, the PSTU, violating the said order, proceeded with the admission process on 10-12-2011.

4. By filing a supplementary-affidavit on 19-2-2012 the UGC stated that in view of the fact that the petitioner No. 1, sibling of Swadhin Chandra Mondal, has already been admitted into the Fishery Department as it appears from the result published on 10-12-2011 and as the petitioner No. 2 is in the waiting list without having any chance to be admitted, they should not have grievance in this regard. It is further stated that to solve the newly created problem the UGC through a meeting with the Vice-Chancellors, Deans and representatives of all the Agricultural Universities as well as all other Universities of Science and Technology of Bangladesh, presided over by Dr AK Azad Chowdhury, the Chairman of the UGC, formed a 7 (seven) member committee to enquire into the matter and the impugned decision was taken.

5. By filing a further supplementary-affidavit on 8-3-12 the UGC, (the respondent Nos. 1, 4 and 6) has further stated that although for last 50 years the Animal Husbandry graduates are working in our country with an aim to increase livestock production, the output of their efforts is insignificant and, in view of the matter, a different department in a public University for Animal Husbandary is not required to be opened. It is further stated that most of the countries of the world, except in some universities, do not offer BSc degree in Animal Husbandry independently as the Animal Husbandry courses are the part of the Veterinary degree. It is further stated that department of Livestock Services is the ultimate job station for both DVM and BSc Animal Husbandry (Hons.) degree holders and though at BSc entry level there are separate posts for the aforesaid two degree holders, at senior level their posts get merged into one resulting in a serious conflicts among them. It was further stated that the petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 did not sit for Animal Husbandry examination at all. In the supplementary-affidavit an allegation has been made that an Assistant Professor named Dr Md Anisur Rahman was insulted by the Vice-Chancellor of the PSTU for requesting the VC of the PSTU to maintain status-quo order of this Court as to admission of the students.

6. The respondent Nos. 8 and 9, the Vice President and Secretary of Bangladesh Veterinary Association respectively, though filed separate affidavit-in-opposition but their contents are same to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by UGC and all that they have stated in their affidavit-in-opposition is that opening up of the department for Animal Husbandary is not necessary at all in view of the current requirement of this kind of graduation in Bangladesh.

7. The respondent No. 2 and 5, the Vice Chancellor and Registrar of the PSTU, filed and affidavit-in-reply to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the UGC and from the contents of the same it appears that they have not opposed the Rule, rather they have justified their actions in commencing admission process and subsequently completing the same.

8. The added respondent Nos. 10-19, who are the admitted students for this academic year in the Department of Animal Husbandry (Honours) Course and has adversely been affected by the interim order passed by this Court, have totally supported the case of the petitioners.

9. Mr Md Badruddoza, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that PSTU is a statutory body, which has been created by পটুয়াখালী বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তি বিশ্ব বিদ্যালয় আইন, ২০০১” (hereinafter referred to as the Ain, 2001) and the University Grants Commission is also a statutory body, which has been created by the University Grants Commissions of Bangladesh Order, 1973 (hereinafter would be referred to as the UGC Order, 1973). Then he places before us Section 4 (ক) and (খ) of the Ain, 2001, which run as follows : —

৪। বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের ক্ষমতা-এই আইন এবং মঞ্জুরী কমিশন আদেশের বিধান সাপেক্ষে, বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের নিম্নবর্ণিত ক্ষমতা থাকিবে, যথা:-

(ক) বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তি বিষয়ে স্নাতক এবং স্নাতকোত্তর পর্যায়ে এবং বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় কর্তৃক বাছাইকৃত আধুনিক বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তির ক্ষেত্রে গবেষনা, জ্ঞানের উৎকর্ষ সাধন ও জ্ঞান বিতরনের ব্যবস্থা করা,

(খ) বিভাগ এবং ইনস্টিটিউটে শিক্ষাদানের জন্য পাঠক্রম নির্ধারন করা,

10. Then he places before us Article 5 of the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh Order, 1973, which runs as follows :—

5. (1) The Commission shall-

(a) assess the needs in the field of University education and formulate plans for the development of such education;

(b) determine the financial needs of the Universities;

(c) receive funds from the Government and allocate and disburse, out of such funds, grants to the Universities for their maintenance and development;

(d) evaluate the programmes under implementation for development of University teaching departments, institutions and other constituent institutions;

(e) examine all kinds of University development plans;

(f) collect statistical and other information on university matters;

(g) advise the Government on the establishment of new Universities or on proposals for expansion of the existing Universities;

(h) advise the Government on proposals to grant the right to confer special degree-awarding status on college which may be considered suitable for such status;

(i) exercise such other powers and perform such other functions as may be conferred on it by any law or by the Government.

11. Upon placing the same, he submits that Section 4(ক) of the Ain, 2001 vests power in the PSTU to make necessary arrangements for education at Honours and Masters level in the field of Science and technology while Section 4(খ) empowers it to ascertain the curriculum and syllabus for each of its department and Institute. He further submits that since the aforesaid powers are to be exercised subject to the provisions laid down in this Act of 2001 and the UGC Order, 2973, the PSTU, accordingly, has exercised the power in opening up its new Department of Animal Husbandry at Honours level in order to offer BSc (Hons) Degree. Mr Bodruddoza continues to submit that the UGC Order, 1973 vests powers in the UGC to assist and co-ordinate the affairs of the universities within Bangladesh but not to boss around the  functions of the universities inasmuch as, both of them are the statutory bodies having equal status in the eye of law. He submits that the UGC acted bonafide and in accordance with law at the time of permitting the PSTU on 29-9-2011 to open up the new Department but its subsequent action in suspending its approval on 20-10-2011 is vitiated by malafide inasmuch as, the same has been done at the behest of a vested quarter, namely BVA, which has been conspiring against the graduates of Animal Husbandry since for long. He submits that the BVA, being envious of the graduates of Animal Husbandry, has been opposing to the expansion of the other branches of this important field of science. He submits that the syllabuses and curriculum of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Medicine are quite different for the two degree courses though the duration of the courses for both the degrees are 4 years but the internship course of the DVM degree holder is of one year whereas the training course for the graduate in Animal Husbandry is of 6 months. He submits that the job and functions of the graduates in Animal Husbandry are completely different from those of the veterinary Doctors in light of the fact that the formers are engaged in the production of animals while the latter are playing the role of physician and surgeon for the animals. He refers to a Gazette notification by which the PSC Rules, 1982, has been amended, (Annexure-E to the affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioners) and submits that the entry points in cadre service for both the groups of graduates are different. Mr Badruddoza submits that the UGC ought not to have acted being instigated by an interested group who evidently possess an ill motive of non-expansion of this specialized education in Animal Husbandry though demands of the BSc (Hons) degree holders are high in our country because of the government's persistent efforts in increasing the animal production. He submits that since the petitioners and other students have already got admitted in Animal Husbandry Department with an expectation to pursue the Degree (Hons) course and the PSTU has made all necessary arrangements for commencing this academic year for 30 students, the UGC was wrong to suspend its approval, which had been granted by it earlier. He submits that the UGC could have carried out its enquiry as to the veracity of the alleged wrong information provided by the BVA without suspending its approval order. He finally submits that the UGC failed to live upto its commitment as to the completion of its inquiry tasks within a week, even if the action of the UGC in passing the impugned suspension order is conceded without being prejudiced. He submits that, here is this case, though the UGC asked its 7 member committee to submit its report within a week, the said committee has failed to submit any report till date.

12. On the other hand, Mr Mahbubey Alam, the learned Senior Counsel appearing with Mr ABM Bayezid on behalf of the respondents No. 1, 4 & 6 submits that the UGC is the final authority to grant permission for opening up any new Department in any university. He submits that the initial permission was obtained by the PSTU from the UGC through providing incorrect information and by suppressing the fact as to the duration of the proposed Honours Course in Animal Husbandry and when the UGC came to know that opening up of the aforesaid course of 4.5 years would create anomalies in this particular field of science, it suspended its approval. Mr Alam submits that the suspension order is aimed at investigating into the allegations raised by the BVA and for that purpose, the UGC has already formed a 7 member committee and upon receiving report from the aforesaid committee, the UGC will either grant permission to the PSTU to continue with the programmer or ask the PSTU to close down the new Department. He submits that the PSTU should not have proceeded with opening up of the Animal Husbandry Department so hurriedly within a span of 3 weeks as could be noticed from the fact that the approval was granted only on 29-9-2011 and the same was withdrawn on 20-10-2011. He further submits that the PSTU ought not to have completed the admission process on 26-1-2012 as on the same day the order of stay was vacated and the PSTU was directed to maintain status quo. He lastly submits that since the UGC has formed a 7 member committee to enquire into the allegation raised by the BVA, the PSTU should have waited for the final decision of the UGC.

13. Mr Haron-or-Rashid, the learned advocate appearing for the respondent No. 8 and 9 submits that the graduates with BSc in veterinary degree, who are known as Doctor in Veterinary Medicine, are very ably managing both the animal health as well as animal production of our country and there is no need to open up separate branch for animal production by introducing BSc (Hons) in Animal Husbandry. He further submits that DVM course is of five years whereas the BSc in Animal Husbandry is a course of 4.5 years and the aforesaid anomaly would lead to a chaos when they will apply for registration in Bangladesh Veterinary Council.

14. Mr Subrata Chowdhury, the learned advocate appearing for the respondent Nos. 2 and 5, submits that the PSTU is situated in the remote area of Bangladesh, which is a suitable place for conducting laboratory works and carrying out researches in Animal production. He submits that the SPTU has met up all the requirements for opening up the Department of Animal Husbandary at Honours level and the UGC issued its clearance having been satisfied as to the feasibility of the opening up of the said Department. He further submits that for this new Department the PSTU has completed the admission of all its students, who are 30 in number, for this academic year on 26-1-2012 before noon by dint of the order of stay on the impugned suspension order passed by this Hon'ble Court and the same was brought to the notice of this Hon'ble Court when the application for vacating the order of stay was moved by the UGC on 26-1-2012 in the afternoon and, therefore, the claim of the UGC that the admission process has been completed flouting the order of status quo is baseless. He lastly submits that since the PSTU has completed admission of 30 students of its new Department on the basis of the approval of the UGC and, further, in view of the admitted fact that the impugned suspension order was issued based on the protest of a vested quarter, the same should be declared illegal by this Hon'ble Court.

15. In reply to the submission made by the UGC and respondents No. 8 and 9 with regard to their apprehension as to creating chaos in getting registered with Bangladesh Veterinary Council after completing 4.5 years BSc course in Animal Husbandry, Mr Badruddoza makes it clear that the petitioner No. 3 representing the association of Animal Husbandry and the members of this Samity do not wish nor they require to get registered with Bangladesh Veterinary Council.

16. It appears that the PSTU is a statutory body created by an act of Parliament, namely “ পটুয়াখালী বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় আইন, ২০১১” As per this statute, the University apparently is an independent body though it requires permission of the University Grants Commission in undertaking and carrying out some specific functions as prescribed in this law. As per section 409, the PSTU is required to seek prior approval from the UGC before opening up a new department. It appears that the PSTU has initiated to open this new department after observing all the necessary formalities. PSTU started admission process and the local Member of Parliament recommended for opening up this new department and the Ministry of Education forwarded recommendation to the UGC for opening up this new department and accordingly admission process was started. It appears that the UGC took a "U" turn and issued the impugned letter upon receiving an objection from the BVA, an association of the Veterinary Doctors of Bangladesh, who are apparently jealous of the graduates in Animal Husbandry and has been influencing the government and other universities not to open up BSc (Hons.) course for Animal Husbandry department for decades and, in the present case as well, the said BVA having impleaded themselves as respondent Nos. 8 and 9, is vehemently opposing the petitioners. Apparently the impugned letter has been issued for the reason as stated in the impugned letter “ সৃষ্ট জটিলতা নিরশন করে” but no explanation as to the preceding Bengali words have been provided in the impugned letter. It further appears that the UGC for the information of all concerned issued a "Press Release" and notified that for resolving the prevailing problematic situation it has formed a 7 member committee which is required to submit its report to the UGC within 7(seven) days. It further appears that till date the said committee did not submit the report nor the UGC has asked to committee to submit the same though six months has passed by now. In the affidavit-in-opposition and supplementary affidavit-in-opposition nothing has been mentioned about the function of the enquiry committee as to whether they have at all started functioning or they have prepared any report as per the instructions of the UGC. From the contents of the affidavit-in-opposition and submission advanced by the learned advocates for the UGC all that we can understand is that the reason for withdrawal of the initial decision is to enquire into the information, which the PSTU has already provided to the UGC at the time of obtaining the approval as to whether opening up the course is suitable and the terms of the course would be of 5 years or four and half years.

17. From the concurrent reading of section 4(ক), and 4(খ), of “পটুয়াখালী বিজ্ঞান ও প্রযুক্তি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় আইন, ২০০১” and Article 5 of the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh Order, 1973, we find that the power of the PSTU in opening up a new Department is subject to the approval of the UGC and the PSTU has commenced the program upon receiving the approval from the UGC. Now the Question as to whether the UGC acted legally in suspending its approval at a time when the PSTU has commenced its admission' process is required to be examined by this Court.

18. It transpires from Annexure C to the Affidavit-in-Reply filed by the petitioners that there is a need of graduates in Animal Husbandry in our country. We find that PSTU is located in a place which is conducive to carry out the research program on animals. In light of the fact that animal Husbandry is related to animal production, breeding, feeding, care and management of dairy and poultry, processing, preservation and marketing of livestock products whereas the jobs and duties of the Veterinary Doctors are related to taking care of the health of the animals, we find that the functions of the two disciplines are quite different. Furthermore, the Animal Husbandry graduates compete in the BCS examinations for different posts as they are accommodated by two separate cadres in the civil service and, thus, there should not be any conflict between the Veterinary Doctors and the graduates in Animal Husbandry. Therefore, we find the protest made by the BVA is undesirable as their activities are directed at creating a monopoly in the field of education on Animal health and Animal production. As such, we hold that issuance of the impugned order by the UGC at the influence of the BVA in suspending its own decision is not in accordance with law. It is pertinent to observe that the UGC, in order to fulfill any lacuna in the duration of course of Animal Husbandry as to whether it should be 5 years or 4.5 years, or to include or exclude any syllabus, could have asked the PSTU to comply with its suggestion instead of forming a committee upon suspending its approval. Further, we find that since the UGC could not obtain any report or suggestion from the said committee till date, the UGC was wrong in taking the decision of suspension of its own approval granted earlier. With regard to the contention of the UGC and added respondent Nos. 8 and 9 that the Animal Husbandry Graduates are not eligible to be registered with the Bangladesh Veterinary Council due to not having similar duration i.e. a 5 year course at Honours level, we find the precedent contentions to be mere an illogical apprehension by the BVA for the reason that there is no scope for the graduates in Animal Hustandry to be registered with the aforesaid Bangladesh Veterinary Council as on behalf of the petitioner No. 3 (Animal Husbandry Association-AHA) it has been categorically submitted before this Court that they do not wish to be associated with the Bangladesh Veterinary Council.

<u>19. Thus, in the present case, we find that the BVA, the association of the Veterinary Doctors, has taken a serious stand against opening up of a separate Honours course relating to animal production albeit this field of education is completely different from the DVM course. It transpires from the statements made by the respondents in their affidavits as well as from the submissions advanced by the learned advocates for the respondents Nos. 8 and 9, which reflects the demeanor of the respondents, that in the absence of sufficient graduates from Animal Husbandry education, the Veterinary Doctors are carrying out the functions of the Animal Husbandry graduates having established a monopoly in the sector of both "animal health" and "animal production" and, as such, they have been endeavoring vehemently to resist any initiative taken in opening up of a Degree level course in Animal Husbandry and in this case as well, as a part of the aforesaid drive, the BVA has successfully persuaded the UGC to suspend its order, granted by itself earlier, for opening up of the Department for Animal Husbandry even the PSTU, by the time of issuance the impugned order by the UGC, has almost completed the tasks of opening up the said new department and the prospective students were expecting to be admitted therein. The UGC being a statutory body ought to have acted independently, not being influenced or biased by the BVA. More importantly, since the UGC was aware that the impugned order not only would affect the interest of the PSTU adversely but also would lead the future of the potential students to an uncertainty, they should have used their prudence reasonably and fairly before issuing such a drastic order. Thus, we hold that the impugned order has lost its validity due to being unduly influenced by the BVA. On any issue, if a decision is taken by any government or statutory body being unduly influenced by a third party, whose role seems to be questionable in the issue that is being dealt with by the authority, the decision loses its efficacy being vitiated by the blame of biasness.</u>

20. Thus, we find a good deal of forces in the submission made by the learned advocate for the petitioner and, accordingly, we find merit in the Rule.

21. In the result, the rule is made absolute.

22. Accordingly, the impugned memo No. UGC/Admin/pabo, Bishwa/402(Tadanto?/08 /8820 dated 25-10-2011 is declared to have been issued without lawful authority and the same has no legal effect.

23. The order of status quo, granted by this Court earlier, is hereby vacated. The students, who already got admitted in the BSc in Animal Husbandry (Hons) course in the Patuakhali Science and Technology University be allowed to continue with their regular studies accordingly.

However, there shall be no order as to costs.

End.

full_judgment:
The plaintiff has filed this suit under the Admiralty Act, 2000, stating, amongst other, that the plaintiff is a private company limited by shares having its registered office at Dhaka and mainly carrying on import and manufacturing business; that the defendant No. 5 is the vessel, owned by defendant No. 9 company incorporated in India, which was incorporated in India and was carrying 10,000 metric tons (MT) of the Sodium Chloride (Industrial Grade) for the plaintiff. However, in connivance with its local agent i.e. Defendant No. 7 and other interested quarter she ran away from the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court delivering only 8,600 MT of goods. The HS Code of the goods is 2501.00.21; that defendant No. 1 is another vessel which is also owned by the defendant No. 9. Defendant No. 2 is the master of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope'. Defendant No. 2 is the master of the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and defendant No. 3 is the local agent of defendant No. 9 for Defendant No. 1 vessel; that both the vessels i.e. Defendant No.1 and 5 vessels are owned by the defendant No. 9; that the plaintiff contracted with their Indian counterpart to import 10,000 MT of Sodium Chloride (Industrial Grade) against irrevocable Letter of Credit (LC) No. 079806010023 (26-1-2006), 079806010024 (29-1-2006), 079806010025 (29-1-2006), 079806010027 (31-1-2006) and 079806010030 (01-2-2006), that each LC was issued for importing 2,000 MT of Sodium Chloride; that accordingly the Indian counterpart of the plaintiff shipped 10,000 MT of Sodium Chloride in the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and her local agent through a letter dated 08-2-2006 severed a NOTICE OF READINESS to the plaintiff informing that the said vessel was due to arrive at Chittagong outer anchorage on 10-2-2006 with 10,000 MT of Sodium Chloride; that however the vessel arrived at the outer anchorage of Chittagong port on 13-2-2006 and started discharging of the said goods on 21-3-2006 at about 01-10 Hours; that during discharging of the said goods the plaintiff came to know that more than a thousand ton of goods were missing from the vessel or was not there; that the plaintiff informed the person concerned however was assured that the owner of the vessel would come to Bangladesh to resolve the issue; that the plaintiff has paid all the required fees including custom duties for 10,000 MT of goods and unloaded only 8,600 MT and was waiting for the owner of the vessel to come to avoid any legal proceedings against the vessel; that the plaintiff was somewhat surprised to learn that on 2.4.2006 the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' left territorial jurisdiction of Bangladesh. Immediately they contacted Chittagong Port authority to know about the present position of the vessel however was shocked to learn from the control room that no one knows the whereabouts of the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart'; that more surprisingly Defendant No. 7 is refusing to answer any telephone call of the plaintiff; that market value of one metric ton of Sodium Chloride today is Tk. 6,850 hence the total value of 1,400 MT of goods is Tk. 95,90,000; that the plaintiff came to know that on 10-4-2006 another vessel i.e. Defendant. No. 1 which also owned by the defendant No. 9 has arrived at the outer anchorage of the Chittagong Port; that the defendant No. 9 has no other asset or property movable or immovable except vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' i.e. Defendant No. 1 within the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court to satisfy any decree which may be given in favour of the plaintiff; that the vessel defendant No. 1 and her owner that is defendant No. 9 is lawfully liable to satisfy the claim of the plaintiff with 18% interest but they have failed to settle the claim; that the defendant No. 1 i.e. 'MV Ocean Hope' entered Bangladesh territorial water on 10-4-2006 and is within the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble court; that the defendant No. 5, the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and her owner i.e. Defendant No. 9 has been neglecting and avoiding the claim of the plaintiff and already left the territorial water of Bangladesh to avoid arrest by this Hon'ble Court and unless an order of arrest is passed by this Hon'ble Court against the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' before she leaves, Bangladeshi territorial water the plaintiff would highly be prejudiced; that the claim against the defendants is a maritime lien against the vessel and it runs with the vessel wherever it goes; that it is necessary for the ends of justice, before the said defendant 1 vessel i.e. 'MV Ocean Hope' changes her nature and character or sails out of Chittagong Port, an warrant of arrest be issued against the said vessel now lying at Chittagong Port, Chittagong and be held in custody by the order of this Hon'ble Court as security for the claimed amount by the defendants to the plaintiff; that in the event of the defendants furnishing sufficient and proper security in favour of the plaintiff in Bangladesh to the satisfaction of this Hon'ble Court, the said vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' may be released from arrest; that unless this Hon'ble Court directs attachment and arrest of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' at present lying at Chittagong Port, Khulna, and the plaintiff would suffer substantial loss and would be seriously prejudiced and, on these allegations, the plaintiff has prayed for a decree for Tk. 95,90,000 against the defendants with 18% interest.

2. Defendant Nos. 1-4 has filed written statement denying all materials allegations made in the plaint and further stating that, the statements made in paragraph 2 of the plaint that the defendant No. 5 is the vessel owned by the defendant No. 9 Company incorporated in India which was carrying 10,000 metric tons sodium chloride (industrial Grade) for the plaintiff or that however in collusion with the local agent i.e. defendant No. 7 and other interested quarter she ran away from the jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court delivering only 8,600 metric tons of goods or that H.S. Code of the goods is 2501.00.24 are beyond the knowledge of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4; that the statements made in paragraph No. 3 of the plaint that the defendant No. 1 is another vessel which is also owned by the defendant No. 9 or that the defendant No. 3 is the local agent of the defendant No. 9 for the defendant No. 1 vessel are not admitted and, as such, denied hereby. That the statement made in paragraph 3 of the plaint that the defendant No. 6 is the Master of the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' is beyond the knowledge of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4; that the statements made in paragraph 4 of the plaint that both the vessels i.e. defendant Nos. 1 and 5 vessels are owned by the defendant No. 9 are not admitted and, as such, denied hereby; that on perusal of the plaint it will be seen that no cause of action is disclosed against the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope and her owners and, as such, the suit against the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 is not maintainable and the order of arrest of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' dated 12-4-2006 is liable to be vacated; that it is stated that the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' is owned by Green Land Shipping Limited and the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' is owned by Longterm Shipping Limited and admittedly there is no contract of carriage between the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' and her owners and the plaintiff and the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope and her owners are not connected with the alleged cause of action of the plaintiff in any way whatsoever and the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' and her owners are under no obligation to pay any alleged claim of the plaintiff and, as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1 and 4; that it is submitted that Sections 4, 4(a) and (b) of the Admiralty Court Act, 2000 provides as follows:

"4. In the case of any such claim as is mentioned in Clauses (d) to (q) of sub-section (2) of section 3 of this Act, being a claim arising in connection with a ship, where the person who would be liable on the claim in an action in person was, when the cause of action arose, the owner or charterer of, or in possession or in control of, the ship, the Admiralty jurisdiction of the High Court Division as the court of Admiralty may (whether the claim gives rise to a maritime lien on the ship or not) be invoked by an action in rem against—

(a) that ship, if at the time when the action is brought it is beneficially owned as respects all the shares therein by that person; or

(b) any other ship which, at the time when the action is brought, is beneficially owned as aforesaid," that it is submitted that the beneficial owner of the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and 'MV Ocean Hope' are totally different and hence the admiralty jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court cannot be invoked by an action. in rem by the plaintiff against the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' for its claim against the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and, as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1 and 4; that it is submitted that due to wrongful arrest of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope', the owners of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' have suffered huge losses and damages and the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 reserve their right to claim appropriate losses and damages from the plaintiff in this regard; that the statements made in paragraphs 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the plaint are not admitted and, as such, denied hereby. It is reiterated that the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 are not connected with the alleged claim of the plaintiff and, as such, they are not liable for the same and hence the suit is liable to be dismissed against the defendant Nos. 1 and 4; that the statements made in paragraph 12 of the plaint that the plaintiff came to know that on 10-4-2006 another vessel i.e. the defendant No. 1 which is also owned by the defendant No. 9 has arrived at the outer anchorage of Chittagong Port are not admitted and, as such, denied hereby; that with regard to the statement made in paragraph 13 of the plaint it is stated that defendant No.1 is not owned by defendant No. 9; that with regard to the statements made in paragraph 14 of the plaint that the vessel defendant No. 1 and her owners i.e. the defendant No. 9 is lawfully liable to satisfy the claim of the plaintiff with 18% interest but they have failed to settle the claim it is stated that the defendant No. 1 is not in any way connected with the alleged cause of action of the plaintiff and the defendant No. 1 i.e. 'MV Ocean Hope' is not owned by defendant No. 9 and, as such, the defendant No. 1 and her owners are not at all liable to satisfy any claim of the plaintiff; that it is stated that the Registration Certificate of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' would shows that the beneficial owner of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' is Longterm Shipping Limited and, as such, the statement of the plaintiff that the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' is owned by Leo Shipping Private Limited India is false and totally baseless and hence denied hereby. It is reiterated that the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' and her owners are in no way liable to settle the alleged claim of the plaintiff; that the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 therefore pray for—

i) dismissal of the suit against the defendant Nos. 1 and 4;

ii) return of the Bank Guarantee being No. 864/CG6600544 dated 26-4-2006 for Tk. 95,90,000 issued by Standard Chartered Bank (SCB), 2 Dilkusha Commercial Area, Dhaka-1000, Bangladesh to the concerned Bank for cancellation;

iii) costs in favour of the defendant Nos. 1 and 4;

iv) any other relief or reliefs that the defendant Nos. 1 and 4 are entitled to under law and equity.

3. Defendant No. 7 has also appeared in the suit and filed a separate written statement denying all materials allegation and further alleging that it is the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' is owned by Greenland Shipping Limited of St. Vincent and the Grenadines who chartered the same to Gujrat Cheminex Limited, India, and the defendant No. 7, Sigma Shipping Lines acted as the said Charterer Gujarat Cheminex Limited's agent for defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' when it arrived at the port of Chittagong; that it is submitted that the said owner Greenland Shipping Ltd or the said charterer, Gujarat Cheminex Ltd of the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart', on whose behalf this defendant No. 7 acted as the Charterer's agent of the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart', are necessary parties in the present suit as being the principal of the defendant No. 7, but they have not been made parties in the present suit and, as such, the present suit is not maintainable for defect of necessary parties and the same is liable to be dismissed; that it is stated that section 4(1) and 4(4) of the Admiralty Courts Act, 2000 provides as follows:-

“৪ ৷ এডমিরাল কোর্টরুপে হাইকোর্ট বিভাগের এখতিয়ার প্ৰয়োগের পদ্ধতি ৷-(১) ধারা ৫ এর বিধান সাপেক্ষে, হইিকোর্ট বিভাগের এডমিরালটি এখতিয়ার সবম্স ক্ষেত্রে action in personam এর মাধ্যমে প্রয়োগ করা যাইবে ৷

(২) ------

(৩) ------

(৪) ধারা ৩ এর উপ-ধারা (২) এর দফা (ঘ) হইতে (থ) তে উল্লেখিত কোন জাহাজ সম্পর্কিত কোন দাৰীর ক্ষেত্রে যে ব্যক্তি মামলার কারণ উত্তরের সময় উক্ত জাহাজের মালিক বা ভাড়াকারী বা দখলকার বা নিয়ন্ত্রনকারী হিসাবে action in personam এ দায়ী থাকেন, সে ক্ষেত্রে, জাহাজটির উপর সামুদ্রিক পূর্বম্বত্বের প্রশ্ন উত্থাপিত হইক বা না হইক এডমিরালটি কোর্ট হিসাবে এডমিরালটি এখতিয়াওে নিম্নবর্ণিত জাহাজের বিরুদ্ধে action in personam আনয়ন করা যইিবে, যথাঃ-

(ক) যদি মামলা আনয়ন করিবার সময় উক্ত জাহাজের সকল শেয়ারের উপর উক্ত ব্যক্তির লাভজনক (beneficial) মালিকানায় থাকে; বা

(খ) যদি মামলা কবিবার সময় অন্য কোন জাহাজ পূর্বোক্তরূপে উক্ত ব্যক্তির লাভজনক (beneficial)মালিকানায় থাকে ৷”

that in view of the above position of law it is respectfully submitted that at the date of the alleged cause of actions and the institution of the present admiralty suit the aforesaid owner Greenland Shipping Ltd. and/or the charterer Gujarat Cheminex Ltd were the beneficial owners of the defendant No. 5 vessel, 'MV Ocean Heart', but they have admittedly not been made parties in the present admiralty suit and, as such, the Admiralty Jurisdiction of this Hon'ble Court cannot be invoked by an action in rem or persona against this defendant No. 7 and the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and, as such, the same is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed; that it is stated that the concerned Bill of Leading was subject to all terms and conditions of the governing Charter party and any addenda thereto and as per the charter Party Agreement it was the responsibility of the consignee for arranging discharge of cargo by lighter vessel; that it is further submitted that the entire cargo of the plaintiff-consignee was duly discharged and delivered to the lightened vessel engaged by the plaintiff-consignee at this time risk and expenses; that the defendant No. 7 therefore prays:

i. for dismissal of the suit against the defendant No. 7;

ii. for cost in favour of the defendant No. 7; and/or

iii. for any other relief or reliefs that the defendant is entitled to under law and equity.

4. Defendant No. 9 has also appeared in the suit and filed written statement denying all materials allegations and further stating that it is stated that this defendant No. 9, Leo Shipping pvt. Limited is not the owner of the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' and the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' and, as such, this defendant No. 9 has no nexus or relationship with the alleged claim of compensation for the alleged non delivery of goods by the defendant not 5 vessel, 'MV Ocean Heart' and this defendant has been unnecessarily impleaded in this suit with malafide intent and, as such, the present suit is liable to be dis-missed against this defendant No. 9 for want of any cause of actins against it; that it is stated that the defendant No. 1 vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' is owned by Long Term Shipping Limited and the defendant No. 5 vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' is owned by Greenland Shipping Limited of St. Vincent & the Grenadines and, as such, they are necessary parties in the present suit but they have not been made parties in the present suit and, as such, the present suit is not maintainable for defect of necessary parties; that the defendant No. 7 therefore prays:

i. for dismissal of the suit against the defendant No. 7;

ii. for cost in favour of the defendant No. 7; and/or

iii. for any other relief or reliefs that the defendant is entitled to under law and equity.

5. The plaintiff has adduced PW 1 (Bishawjit Kumar Saha) and PW 2 (Captain Rafiqul Islam), whereas defendant Nos.1 and 4, filing joint written statement, have adduced DW 1 (AHM Mahfuzur Rahman), which the defendant No. 7 has adduced DW 2 (Sheikh Mohammed Rafiqul Islam Bablu) as well as the parties have exhibited certain the documents in support of their respective cases, which are in the record before this court.

6. The point for determination in this case decide as to whether the plaintiff is entitled to the relief prayed for.

7. The learned Advocate Mr. M. Moksudul Islam, appearing for the plaintiff, submits that exhibits J and J-1 (both marked with objection), duly proved by PW 1, clearly show that the defendant No. 1 ('MV Ocean Hope') and defendant No. 5 ('MV Ocean Heart') are owned by defendant No. 9 (Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd). He further submits that the defendant No. 5, with-out discharging the Cargo imported from India, in full, has fled away from the Chittagong Port. Thereafter, another vessel ('MV Ocean Hope'/ Defendant No. 1) owned by defendant No. 9, having called on Chittagong Port, this suit has been filed and order of arrest (of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope') was passed by this court. However, subsequently, by furnishing security they said vessel was released from arrest. He also submits that exhibit-J and J-1, on which defendants relied to show that defendant Nos. 1 and 5 are not owned by defendant No. 9, are not admissible in evidence for the reason that neither of the same is issued either in English or in Bangla i.e. in any language intelligible to this court. Besides, he further submits, that those documents are not authenticated by any authorized person, like Bangladesh consul at the place of registration. He next submits that a mere comparison of the signatures appearing on Exhibit C and Cl, D and D1 would show that these are not matching and that these are fabricated for the purpose of the defence taken in this suit. He finally submits that, the Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd is the operator as well as the owner of the two defendant vessels and that the plaintiff has, by adducing oral and documentary evidence, adequately proved his case for getting the decree prayed for in the plaint.

8. The learned Advocate Mr. Ahsanul Karim alongwith Mr. .Mohammad Ohiullah, appearing for defendant Nos. 1-4, having drawn my attention to the pleadings of the parties as well as to the evidence on record, firstly submits that the Bill of Leading (BL), exhibit-E series, and the Bill of Entry, exhibit-F series, evidently show that the defendant Nos. 1-4 is not the carrier of the Cargo in question. Nor this is the case of the plaintiff. On the other hand, he continues, that exhibit J and J1, issued by the competent authority, clearly and apparently show that these are not certificates of registration, rather these are "international ship security certificates" issued to Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd (defendant No. 9) as it was entrusted with the security administration of safety and measures of the concerned vessels and that the owner of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' is not the defendant No. 9, but Long Term Shipping Ltd. He then; referring to exhibit J and J1, further submits that these two documents refer to the name of the company, namely Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd. (defendant No. 9) and it has no nexus with the ownership of the vessel. The name of the owner of a vessel is to be recorded in her registration certificate and this law is known to as well as uniform worldwide, he further adds. Next, referring to the deposition of PW 1, the learned Advocate submits that the PW 1 has also admitted that this exhibit J and J1 are not documents of ownership of the vessel, defendant No. 1. As such, referring to the documentary and oral evidence, he submits, it has been established that defendant No. 1-4 has no nexus with defendant No. 9 and that 'MV Ocean Hope' or 'MV Ocean Heart' are not owned by defendant No. 9 and that the plaintiff has utterly failed to discharge the onus to prove his case. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost and the bank guarantee furnished on behalf defendant No. 1 shall be returned to her owner or authorized agent.

9. The learned Advocate Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, appearing for the defendant No. 7, submits that the defendant No. 5 is not owned by defendant No. 9, but by Green Land Shipping Ltd. There is no evidence on record, which is lying before this court, to show that the defendant No.7 is an agent of defendant No. 5. He next submits that the defendant No. 7 is the agent of the chatterer namely, Gujarat Cheminex Ltd, who has chartered 'MV Ocean Heart' (defendant No. 5) and not of defendant No. 9. Besides, this defendant has disclosed that he is the agent of the charterer Gujarat Chaminex Ltd. As such, although the defendant No. 7 has disclosed the name of its principal, but the principal was not made party in this suit. Hence, the suit is not maintainable against this defendant, for not impleading the necessary party, in view of the provisions of section 217 of the Contract Act, 1872. Thereafter, the learned lawyer, referring to section 121 of the Evidence Act submits that this PW 1 is not authorized to sign the verification below the plaint, on behalf of the plaintiff. Next, referring to section 6 of the Admiralty Act, 2000, the learned Advocate further submits that the PW 1 is not authorized to sign the verification under that provision as well. As such, the plaint is not properly framed or presented and the entire deposition of PW 1 and 2 is liable to be struck down, the same being inadmissible in evidence. The learned lawyer, referring to exhibit-K(1), submits that the vessel ('MV Ocean Heart') ship has discharged the entire Cargo, except 58 Metric Tons, and her master served notice upon the plaintiff to take delivery of the same. But, the plaintiff did not respond. Hence, in order to avoid demurrage the defendant No. 5 left Chittagong Port with No Objection Certificate (NOC) dated 28-3-2006, issued by the Chittagong Port Authority. In support of his contention, recorded above, the learned Advocate has referred to the decisions reported in 54 DLR 276, 4 BLC 195, 34 DLR 362 (paragraph No. 5 and 6), 54 DLR 612 and 20 DLR (SC) 225 (paragraph No. 14).

10. Learned Advocate Ms. Shahanaj Akther, having appeared on behalf of the defendant No. 9, has adopted the submissions made by the learned lawyers appearing for the defendants Nos. 1-4 and for the defendant No. 7.

11. I have heard the learned Advocates and perused the pleadings submitted by the parties, respectively, as well as the oral and documentary evidence on record.

12. In this case the entire burden lies upon the plaintiff to prove his case and he cannot depend upon the weakness, if any, in the defence case.

13. I have examined the documents marked as Exhibits-E series (the Bill of leading), from which it is abundantly clear that there was no contract of carriage between the defendant No. 1 'MV Ocean Hope') and the plaintiff. Next, having considered exhibit J and J(1), I find that the defendant No. 9 (Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd) was only an operator of the safety and security administration of 'MV Ocean Hope' (defendant No.1) and of 'MV Ocean Heart' (defendant No. 5). Besides, exhibit-(J) and J(1) are both "International Ship Security Certificate", as is clearly evident and intelligible from the expressions/narrations contained in English in these two certificates. I also find that these certificates [exhibits J and J(1)] are not registration certificates of the aforesaid two vessels and that the name of 'Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd' has been shown, in both certificates, as against the name of the company in charge of safety and security administration of these two vessels. Besides, PW 1, during his cross-examination was asked as to whether Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd. was the owner of 'MV Ocean Hope' and in reply the PW 1 has said no.

14. Therefore, this is an admitted position that 'MV Ocean Hope' is not owned by Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd. PW 1, in his cross-examination (by the defendants 1-4) has admitted that exhibits J and J(1) are international security certificate (as distinct from the registration certificates recording ownership of the vessel) and he has also admitted that "The Ship registration certificate is not in the exhibited documents". PW 1 has further admitted, during cross-examination (by defendants 1-4) that, "the name of the owner Leo Shipping Pvt Ltd is not written as owner of the vessel 'MV Ocean Hope' and 'MV Ocean Heart'". He has also admitted that there is no reference to the name of 'MV Ocean Hope' in the Bills of lading (exhibits-E series). While cross-examined by defendant No. 7, PW 1 has admitted that, "The power of attorney is not in the exhibited documents". Whereas, PW 2 has admitted that "I am deposing in the instant admiralty suit as the C & F agent." The defendants suggested that neither PW 1 nor PW 2 had any authority to depose on behalf of the plaintiff and I found no material on record authorizing them to depose on behalf of the plaintiff. DW 2, adduced by defendant No. 7, in this deposition, has stated that they are agent of the charterer of defendant No. 5 vessel (not of the owner). He has also filed and proved the NOC dated 28-3-2006 (exhibit-Ka) that the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' (defendant No. 5) had left Chittagong Port after obtaining NOC and that they have not fled away from the Chittagong Port, as alleged in the plaint. The plaintiff could not discredit his testimony during cross-examination.

15. As such, having considered both oral and documentary evidence, I find that Leo Shipping Pvt. Ltd is not the owner of the vessels 'MV Ocean Hope' or of 'MV Ocean Heart' rather it was in charge of the security and safety administration of these two vessels.

16. Next, considering the deposition given by the DW 1, I find that he has also supported the case of the defendant that the certificates marked as Exhibit J and J1 do not bear the name of the owner of the vessels and that the ship registration certificate (recording ownership of the vessel) is not in the exhibited documents. Besides, I also find that the PW 1 and PW 2 were not duly authorized to depose on behalf of the plaintiff.

17. Having considered the documentary as well as the oral evidence of PW 1 and 2 as well as that of the DW 1 and DW 2, I hold that the plaintiff has failed to prove that defendant No. 1 or 5 is owned by defendant No. 9 as well as he has failed to prove that defendant No. 7 is the agent of defendant No. 9.

18. Then considering the submissions of the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 7, I find that the defendant No. 7 has disclosed the name of his principal, i.e. the Charterer of 'MV Ocean Heart'. In this case the plaintiff ought to have made Gujarate Cheminex Ltd (Chartarer of 'MV Ocean Heart'), the principal of the defendant No. 7, a party in this suit. But, for not making the disclosed principal (Charterer) a party to this case, this case is also defective for non-joinder of necessary party.

<u>19. Besides, I also find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 7 that in the absence of any Power of Attorney to give deposition on behalf of the plaintiff, the entire deposition of the plaintiff's witnesses is not admissible in evidence and in support of his contention, the learned advocate has relied on 54 DLR 276: Shah Alam vs Abul Kalam. It was held in that case that, a power of attorney not executed before or authenticated by a notary public nor any representative of the foreign mission, is not admissible in evidence. It has also been held in that case that, only a duly constituted attorney can represent an absent party. I respectfully concur with the views taken in this decision. I also find that in 34 DLR 362: Albert David vs. Brosterns, it has been held that no decree can be passed against the agent of the charterer (defendant No. 2 in that case) in the absence of the owner of the ship and the charterer, while 54 DLR 612: S. M. Fazlul Haque vs Salauddin it has been held that, no question of agent's liability to any third party for any breach can arise and prima facie any person who can be sued is the principal." The views expressed in these cases support the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the defendant No. 7.</u>

20. Having considered the issues involved in this case as well as the pleadings of the parties and the deposition on record, I find and hold that the plaintiff has failed to prove his case. I also find that the vessel 'MV Ocean Heart' has left Chittagong Port after obtaining NOC issued by Chittagong Port Authority on 28-3-20006 (Exhibit Ka) and that the plaintiff did not receive only 58 Metric tons of Cargo in spite of several reminders, given on behalf of the vessel, to take delivery of the same. For this conduct of the importer the vessel cannot suffer demurrage by remaining detained at Chittagong Port for uncertain time. It has committed no fault in leaving the Chittagong Port, in this situation, with NOC issued by the Chittagong Port on 30-6-2006, Exhibit Ka(1).

Hence I find no merit in this case. In the result this Admiralty Suit is dismissed. The bank concerned is directed return the bank guarantee (No. 864/CG6600544 dated 26-4-2006 issued by the SCB) immediately to the defendant No. 1 or to its authorized agent.

Costs will borne by the parties respectively.

End.

full_judgment:
AFM Ali Asgar J : This rule was issued calling upon the defendant opposite party Nos. 1-4 to show cause as to shy the impugned judgment dated 10-6-1999 and decree dated 20-6-1999 passed by the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, 10th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 211 of 1993 should not be set aside and why the judgment dated 28-4-1993 and decree dated 16-5-1993 passed by the senior Assistant Judge, 1st Additional Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 45 of 1991 should not be restored and such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court might seem fit and proper.

2. At the time of issuance of the rule the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 10-6-1999 was stayed.

3. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the rule in short are that the plaintiff and the defendant No. 4 entered into a contract with the defendant Nos. 1-3 for purchase of the suit property to which defendant Nos. 1-3 agreed to sell and price was settled at Taka 66,000. The plaintiff and defendant No. 4 each paid Taka 28,500 and in total paid Taka 57,000 as earnest money and deed of agreement for sale was executed on 24-12-1988 and it was stipulated that the plaintiff and defendant No. 4 would offer the balance of the consideration to the defendant Nos. 1-3 within one month upon which they would execute and register the sale deed in favour of the plaintiff and defendant No. 4. The plaintiff states that after execution of deed of agreement, the photo copy of the same was kept with the plaintiff and original deed of agreement was taken by the defendant No. 4. The plaintiff allege that he asked the defendant No. 4 to procure remaining balance consideration money of Taka 4,500 and he also requested the defendant Nos. 1-3 to execute and register the sale deed after accepting the balance consideration money in favour of the plaintiff and defendant No. 4. The plaintiff alleged that he made several offers since then but the defendant Nos. 1-3 defered the execution and registration of sale deed and defendant No. 4 deferred the matter on the pretext of procuring his balance consideration money. They plaintiff alleged that thereafter he came to know on 1st. week of April, 1989 that defendant Nos. 1-3 transferred the suit land in favour of the defendant No. 4 in collusion with him without knowledge of the plaintiff. The plaintiff stated that defendant Nos. 1-3 are bound by way of deed of agreement dated 24-12-1988 to transfer the 1st Schedule of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff states that the defendant No. 4 is bound to transfer the second schedule of the suit land in favour of the plaintiff. The plaintiff alleges that the defendant No. 4 has got no right to get the entire suit property transferred in favour of him without knowledge of the plaintiff. The plaintiff states that after having knowledge on 1st week of April, 1989 about the transfer of the entire suit property in favour of the defendant No. 4 by the defendant Nos. 1-3 the plaintiff repeatedly requested to transfer half portion in his favour but they paid no heed to the request of the plaintiff. Hence the plaintiff filed the suit for Specific Performance of Contract.

4. The defendant No. 4 filed a written statement denying material allegations of the plaintiff and alleges that the suit is not maintainable in its present form, the suit is barred by defect of parties, the suit is barred by limitation. The case of the defendant in short is that the defendant Nos. 1-3 entered into agreement with the plaintiff and defendant No. 4 to sell the first schedule of the suit land on 24-12-1988. The defendant states that photo copies of all the documents relating to the suit property and deed of agreement and title deed of defendant No. 1-3 have been hand over to the plaintiff. The defendant states that due to the difficulties of procuring the consideration money but the plaintiff the defendant No. 4 paid entire consideration as was fixed and recited in the deed of agreement. The defendant states that due to failure of the plaintiff to procure consideration money of the deed of agreement, the plaintiff returned original deed of agreement as well as all related documents to the defendant No. 4. The defendant states that after expiry of the duration of the deed of agreement, the defendant Nos. 1-3 expressed their unwillingness to sell the property and, as such, they returned the consideration money relating to the deed of agreement and took back all the documents of ownership as well as photocopies of the documents, also original deed of agreement from the defendant No. 4. The defendant states that, thereafter, defendant Nos. 1-3 freshly settled the price of the first schedule property at Taka 70,000 and after accepting entire consideration money at a time from the defendant No. 4, the defendant Nos. 1- 3 executed and registered Sub-kabala deed on 4-3-1989 in favour of the defendant No. 4 and delivered possession thereof as well as handed over all the related documents of ownership in favour of the defendant No. 4. The defendant allege that the plaintiff on the basis of photo copy of the deed of agreement trying to grab the suit property. The defendant states that plaintiff is neither in possession of the suit schedule property nor he has got any papers in his possession relating to ownership of the suit schedule property. The property is in possession of the defendant No. 4. Hence the defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit with cost.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties the learned Senior Assistant Judge framed as many as 5 issues for adjudication and disposal of the suit. The plaintiff in support of his case adduced 2 witnesses including the plaintiff himself as PW 1 and the defendant No. 4 who is the lone contesting defendant in the suit also adduced 2 witnesses including the defendant No. 4 himself as DW 1. The learned Senior Assistant Judge after conclusion of trial and on hearing the parties and on consideration of evidences on record both oral and documentary was pleased to decree the suit of the plaintiff by his judgment and decree dated 28-4-1993.

6. The contesting defendant No. 4 being aggrieved by the dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge preferred Title Appeal No. 211 of 1993 in the Court of the District Judge, Dhaka which was ultimately on transfer heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, lath Court, Dhaka who after hearing the parties and on perusal of the evidences on record was pleased to allow the appeal and thereby set aside the judgment and decree passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 10-6-1999 (decree signed on 20-6-1999).

7. The plaintiff being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree of reversal passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 10th Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 211 of 1993 as petitioner moved this Court its revisional jurisdiction as per provision of Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, hence this rule.

8. Mr Nikhil Kumar Saha, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has submitted that the impugned judgment is not a proper judgment of reversal as provided under Provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure as the learned Appellate Judge being the last Court of fact did not properly controvert the categorical finding arrived at by the learned trial Judge while decreeing the suit and the learned Appellate Judge did not properly discuss and evaluate the evidences on record in its entirety and correct perspective thus the learned appellate Judge failed in his duty and arrived at wrong finding and decision leading to error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. As such the same is not sustainable in law.

9. Mr Saha next submits that the learned Appellate Judge erred in law in not taking into consideration the fact that conveyance document is a concluded agreement and is binding upon both the parties unless and until it is cancelled. According to Mr Saha here in this case the execution of the deed of agreement is admitted fact and there is no evidence to the effect that the said agreement has been cancelled by the executants. And the same having been enforce the defendant Nos. 1-3 were not legally entitled to transfer the suit property in favour of the defendant No. 4 beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff as the plaintiff and the defendant No. 4 was the joint recipient of the said deed of agreement and the defendant No. 4 was not legally authorized to get the entire suit land transferred in his favour beyond the knowledge of the plaintiff and in conveyance with the defendant Nos. 1-3 taking recourse to deceitful tactic to defraud the plaintiff and the learned Appellate Judge by not considering this very material aspect of the case has committed error of law and fact as well and arrived at an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice. As such the same is not sustainable in law. In support of his argument Mr Saha has referred to a decision of the then Pakistan Supreme Court reported in 14 DLR (SC) 112 being the case of Mohiuddin Mollah vs Province of East Pakistan.

10. Mr. Saha next submits that the defendant Nos. 1-3 did not cancel the deed of agreement by serving any notice in writing or even there is no evidence that even verbally the defendant Nos. 1-3 cancelled the deed of agreement (Bonaparte). So the deed of agreement dated 24-12-1988 was in very much enforce as valid contract and the same being enforce the transfer of the schedule one property to the defendant No. 4 who is a co-purchaser in the contract is quite illegal and the learned Appellate Judge failed to consider this aspect of the case and thereby not considering this very vital aspect of the case the learned Appellate Judge set aside the decree of the trial Court without properly adjudicating this aspect of the case on proper evaluation of the evidences on record as such the impugned judgment is not sustainable in law because the same suffers from non-considering and misreading and non-reading of evidences on record thus the learned Appellate Judge arrived at erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice while he misconstrued the legal position relating to deed of agreement and contract as such the same is not sustainable in law.

11. Mr Saha lastly submits that the learned Appellate Judge being the last Court of fact was 'duty bound to advert to the findings of the learned trial Judge on proper evaluation and discussion of the evidences on record as per provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure but here the learned Appellate Judge failed to do so as he has passed a very short slip judgment without proper discussion and evaluation of the evidence on record and deed of agreement itself as such the impugned judgment is not sustainable in law. He prays that the rule be made absolute.

12. Mr Harendra Nath Nandi, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party has first of all submitted that the plaintiff is to satisfy the Court on four points for getting a decree for Specific Performance of Contract viz i. Contract is to be proved, ii. Question of limitation i.e. time being essence of contract, iii. Payment of consideration money, iv. Demand. He submits that if the plaintiff can satisfy and prove all these four points that he was quite diligent to perform his part of the contract and fulfill all the four points under that circumstances the plaintiff can get a decree for Specific Performance of Contract but according to Mr Nandi here in this case the plaintiff had no right to institute the suit against the defendant No. 4 as because there was no contract for sale and purchase of schedule property between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 4. Moreover, according to Mr Nandi the plaintiff hopelessly failed to comply with the aforesaid four elements for getting a decree for Specific Performance of Contract. He candidly submitted that the plaintiff hopelessly failed to perform his part of obligation as embodied in the contract as such the defendant No. 4 who paid the full earnest money out of the stipulated price and later on by fresh negotiation with the defendant Nos. 1-3 he by paying higher value purchased the suit land on fresh negotiation within the knowledge of the plaintiff as the plaintiff failed to perform his part of obligation as per terms of the deed of agreement and time being the essence of contract.

13. He further submits that since the plaintiff failed to collect the balance consideration money and pay the same to the sellers the plaintiff voluntarily return the deed of agreement and other related papers to the defendant No. 4 and the defendant Nos. 1-3 after expiry of stipulated period of one month return the earnest money to the defendant No. 4 and took back the original deed of agreement and other papers and documents relating to the title of the defendant Nos. 1-3, thus cancelled the deed of agreement and thereafter the defendant No. 4 on a fresh negotiation with the defendant Nos. 1-3 paid Taka 70,000 at a time towards the price of the suit land and got the suit land transfer in his name by registered saf kabala on 4-3-1989 in his favour and the said fact was well within the knowledge of the plaintiff. The plaintiff later on with ulterior motive have filed the suit out of grid with photo copy of the deed of agreement and this fact having been considered by the learned Appellate Judge who reversed the judgment and decree of the learned trial Judge is quite inconformity with the evidences on record as such the impugned judgment is liable to be upheld. In support of his argument Mr Nandi has referred to a decision of our High Court Division in the case of Silva Estate Ltd. vs Abdul Hakim Mia, reported in 43 DLR 360. He prays that the rule be discharged.

<u>14. I have given my anxious consideration to the submission made at the Bar. I have gone through the rule petition, the impugned judgment, the judgment of the trial Court as well as the evidence-on-record both oral and documentary. After going through the impugned judgment I find substance in the submission of Mr Saha to the effect that the learned Appellate Judge failed to deliver the judgment in adherence to the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I find that the learned Appellate Judge passed a very short cut judgment without properly adverting the points and issues that has been decided by the learned trial Judge who on discussion and evaluation of evidences on record arrived at his decision to decree the suit but the learned Appellate Judge miserably failed to make thread bare discussion of the evidences on record and after going through the judgment I find that the learned Appellate Judge only partially discuss the evidences of PW 1 and 2 and he did not evaluate the entire evidence-on-record and I find that the judgment suffers from misreading and non-reading of evidences on record. The learned Appellate Judge being the last Court of fact ought to have advert the categorical finding and decision given by the learned trial Judge in the impugned judgment but here the learned Appellate Judge failed in complying with the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure as such the impugned judgment passed by the learned Appellate Judge is not a proper judgment of reversal as has been decided by our lordships in the Appellate Division in so many decision. Specially the learned Appellate Judge arrived at wrong finding setting aside the judgment of the trial Court that the defendant No. 4 did not take any tactic for getting the sale, deed registered in his name in connivance with the defendant Nos. 1-3 which is not at all the correct finding as I find after going through the evidences on record and pleadings of the parties. I find that this is not correct finding of the learned Appellate Judge rather it is contrary to the evidences on record. On this count the learned Appellate Judge did not properly evaluate the deposition of the two PW's who very stated that the defendant No. 4 who was supposed to collect his portion of the balance consideration money and to inform the plaintiff that he has managed his portion. The defendant No. 4 asked the plaintiff (PW 1) and his corroborated witness PW No. 2 not to do very hurry, he will arrange his balance consideration money soon and then kabala will be registered. The plaintiff as PW 1 and PW 2 stated that they approached the agents /karjakarak of the defendant Nos. 1-3 to get the deed executed in favour of the plaintiff as he has arranged his balance consideration money but the agent/caracara of the defendant Nos. 1-3 asked them to contact the defendant No. 4. In this way the defendant No. 4 and defendant No. 1 and agent/karjakarak of the defendant Nos. 1-3 taking recourse to deceitful tactics to defraud the plaintiff and got the sale deed registered in favour of the defendant No. 4 within one month 7 days time of the expiry of the stipulated period of the deed of agreement. Although the defendant No. 4 tried to establish a case that the plaintiff failed to collect his part of the balance consideration money and therefore he return the original deed of agreement (Bonaparte) and other papers to the defendant Nos. 4 who in his turn return the same to the defendant Nos. 1-3 as they express their unwillingness to executed and registered saf kabala in favour of the plaintiff and defendant No. 4. In view of the fact that the stipulated period for execution and registration of their sale deed has been over and the defendant No. 4 afterwards on separate deal agreed to purchase the case property at a higher price on fresh negotiation with the defendant Nos. 1-3 and accordingly he got the Saf kabala registered in his name alone within the knowledge of the plaintiff. But on scrutiny of the evidence on record I find that there is no such corroborative evidence to support the case of the defendant No. 4. In this respect the evidences of PW 1 and 2 are corroborative and believable but the learned Appellate Judge referring to few lines of deposition of PW 1 and 2 has made his comment that the PW 1 i.e. the plaintiff did not enter into any agreement with the defendant No. 4 and, as such, he was not entitled to get kabala from the defendant No. 4 and referring to the deposition of the plaintiff as PW No.1 and his corroborative witness the PW No. 2 the learned Appellate Judge reversed and set aside the well reasoned and well evaluated judgment of the learned Trial Judge without properly discussing and evaluating the deposition of these two PW's. Thus I find that the learned Appellate Judge did not properly evaluate the evidences on record and the same suffers from the misreading and non-reading of evidences on record. As such the impugned judgment is not sustainable as I find after perusing the evidences on record. Wherein it is admitted position that the plaintiff and the defendant No. 4 have entered into an agreement with the defendant Nos. 1-3 for purchase of the suit property jointly and it is written in the said deed of agreement (Bainapatra) that the purchasers have paid Taka 57,000 as earnest money out of Taka 66,000 fixed as total consideration money for the suit land and the defendant No. 4 was the scribe of the said deed of agreement which is admitted by the defendant No. 4 himself although he tried to establish that the plaintiff could not pay the earnest money of his portion due to shortage of fund but he could not adduce any corroborative evidence to that effect as such the writing of the deed of agreement stands as valid terms and conditions and it is clear from the deed to agreement that both the intending purchaser paid Taka 28,500 each as earnest money to the seller and on receipt on the same amount the executants of the said Bonaparte signed and executed the deed of agreement (Bainapatra).</u>

15. In that view of the matter, the learned Appellate Judge measurably failed to find that the deed of agreement (Bonaparte) being legal and valid deed of agreement (Bainapatra) and the same being admitted position he ought to have concurred with the finding of the learned Trial Judge and there was no scope for him to reverse the judgment and finding of the learned trial Judge in this respect.
