full_judgment:
Nozrul Islam Chowdhury J : First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 Agrani Bank Ltd. (appellant) vs Samsad Asif (respondents) with Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 Agrani Bank vs Goldhil Fibers Ltd. and Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 Sonali Bank vs Agrani Bank. The aforesaid three matters having arisen out of the self same subject matter and in between almost the same parties, those are being disposed of analogously by a single judgment as under :-

First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 arises out of Title Suit No.280 of 1994 which was instituted on 30-11-1994 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka by Agrani Bank Ltd. as plaintiff impleading Shamsad Asif, Nowshad Asif and Ershad Asif as main defendant Nos. 1-3 respectively, while Abidur Rahman, Al-Baraka Bank Ltd. Rajdhani Unnoyun Katripaka, M/s Goldhil Tobaco Complex Ltd. M/s Nippon Traders Ltd. and M/s Nippon Motors Ltd. as pro-defendant Nos.4-10 respectively. The aforesaid defendant Nos. 8-10 were represented by their Managing Director Abidur Rahman who has also been impleaded as defendant No. 4 in the suit. The subject matter involved in the suit is being described as under:-

(1) District Dhaka PS Gulshan Mouza Bhola Shamair at present Gulshan Model Town (RAJUK) plot No. 33 Road No. 144 Block CEN(H) measuring an area of 14 khata and 15 chattak  and the structures available thereon. The suit was instituted seeking a decree:

(a) pro-defendant No. 4 (Abidur Rahman) is the real owner of the suit land

(b) the pro-forma defendant No. 4 having given personal guarantee against the loan he took from the plaintiff bank amounting to a first charge of the bank for the suit land.

(c) the alleged guarantee of the suit land dated 2-6-1990 by the defendant Nos. 1-3 in favour of defendant No. 5 is a sham paper transacting .

2. The suit was instituted by the plaintiff disclosing inter alia in its plaint that the plaintiff is a banking institution constituted under PO 16 of 1972 and engaged in banking business; the defendant No. 4 Abidur Rahman is a renowned business man who is the Managing Director of defendant Nos. 8-10 i.e. M/s. Goldhil Tobaco Complex Ltd. M/s Nippon Traders; and M/s Nippon Motors Ltd; defendant No. 4 used to take loan from the bank upon operating account as the Managing Director of the said Companies in the form of cash credit, over draft , working capital and project loan, letter of credit loan etc. upon executing personal guarantee; on 7-12-1973 the defendant No. 4 purchased the suit land at a consideration of Taka 2(two) lacs by a registered kabala No. 28926 in the benami of his three sons namely the defendant Nos. 1-3 and got possession over the same; thereafter the defendant No. 4 also constructed a two storied building over the suit land upon fraudulently diverting the loan obtained from the bank and the house was constructed at a cost of Taka 30,00,000 and he has been living in the said house with the members of his family including the defendant Nos. 1-3; the defendant Nos. 1-3 being minors in the year 1973 they had no means whatsoever to purchase the suit land; the plaintiff bank granted loan in favour of (b) defendant No. 4 treating him as the owner of the suit land since he had disclosed his ownership of the suit land to the bank on various ways and the bank also granted loan to the defendant No. 4 treating him as the owner of the suit land, moreover the defendant No. 4 did never disclose that the suit land stands in the name of his minor sons as his benamdar; had it been known to the bank that the defendant No. 4 purchased the suit land the benami of his minor sons in that case the plaintiff bank would have obtained personal guarantee from defendant Nos. 1-3 too the plaintiff bank did not know about such transaction until institution of Miscellaneous Case before the 1st court of Subordinate Judge, by the defendant No. 1; the plaintiff bank instituted Money Suit No. 58 of 1991,121 of 1991, 39 of 1992, 25 of 1993, 31 of 1991 and 63 of 1991 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court and Artha Rin Adalat against the defendant No. 4 to the knowledge of all other defendants and obtained decrees in all those suits; thereafter plaintiff bank got money decree execution in Execution Case Nos. 23 of 1993, 24 of 1993, 25 of 1993, 27 of 1993, 31 of 1993 and 32 of 1993 before the Subordinate Judge and 1st Court of Artha Rin Adalat where-upon the suit land was attached and the said attachment has been in force; in course of such attachment of the suit land the defendant Nos. 1-3 brought Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1993 on 30-11-1993, Miscellaneous Case No. 51 of 1993 on 30-11-1993, Miscellaneous Case No. 45 of 1993 on 30-9-1993 , Miscellaneous Case No.47 of 1993 on 30-11-1993 and Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1993 on 30-11-93 under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure laying a false claim of their ownership in the suit land.

3. It is also disclosed in the plaint that the defendant Nos.1-3 fraudulently and in collusion with the defendant No. 4 alleged to have mortgaged the suit land in favour of defendant No.5 by a registered mortgage deed dated 2-6-90 the defendant No. 5 knowing full well about the first charge of the plaintiff bank over the suit land illegally granted loan in favour of defendant Nos.1-3 against the alleged mortgage of the suit land in its favour; as matter of fact the plaintiff bank had obtained 1st charge over the suit land created by virtue of personal guarantee given by the defendant No. 4 against the loan obtained by him from the plaintiff bank; the documents in connection with the suit land having been left in the custody of the defendant No. 5 by defendant Nos.1-3 by way of an alleged mortgage to the defendant No.5 plaintiff bank; therefore as plaintiff prayed for a decree as aforesaid.

4. The defendant Nos.1, 2 and 3 entered appearance upon filing written statement on 13-11-1995 denying the material allegations made in the plaint stating inter alia that the suit land belonged to the answering defendants and the same was purchased in the year 1973 by their maternal grandfather by a registered kabala No. 28926 of 1973 who have been in possession thereof and in course of their business they have obtained loan executing a registered mortgage deed in favour of defendant No. 5 on 2-6-1990 and they had also authorized defendant No. 5 to sell the suit land by way of power of attorney if need be; the answering defendants also mutated their names in respect of the suit land upon payment of rent to the government and the Municipal holding also stands in the name of the answering defendants in respect of the suit property when they are also paying all necessary taxes to the City Corporation against receipts; the answering defendants also disclosed in their written statement to produce the necessary documents of their ownership and possession of the suit land in favour of defendant Nos. 1-3 at the time of hearing; the claim of the plaintiff over the suit land is false and without any basis; hence the suit was liable to be dismissed.

5. The defendant No.5 Al-Baraka Bank upon filing a separate written statement on 17-6-1997 denied the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia that the suit land was leased out to one Mr Tashfin I Huq for 99 years by Dhaka Improvement Trust (DIT) on 6-12-1965 at a consideration of Taka 12,107 and got possession; thereafter said Mr Tashfim I Huq gifted away the property in question in favour of his wife Ms Shahana Huq and the donee got her name recorded with the DIT in respect of the suit land and also constructed a double storied building thereon; in 1973 Ms Shahana Huq transferred the suit property in favour of defendant Nos. 1-3 at a consideration of Taka 2 (two) lacs with prior approval of DIT by a registered deed dated 30-11-1973 and the purchasers got possession and they had also mutated their names in the office of the DLR as leasee thereof; in 1989 one Mr Masudur Rahman proprietor of Masud Enterprise applied for Bai-Muajjal facility of Taka 1.50 crore to defendant Nos. 5 and the facility was sanctioned by defendant No. 5 against collateral security of legal and equitable mortgage of the suit property recorded in the name of the defendant Nos. 1-3; the guarantors of the loan as per rules of DIT and terms of the lease deed (the defendant Nos. 1-3) applied for permission to create legal and equitable mortgage in favour of Al-Baraka Bank (BD) Ltd. and the same was approved by DIT vide Memo dated 7-2-1989; the defendant 1-3 also submitted non encumbrance certificate to defendant No. 5 thereafter registered deed of mortgage dated 2-6-1990 and equitable mortgage by deposing all registered documents with the defendant No. 5 was created; the defendant Nos. 1-3 also executed a registered irrevocable general power of attorney dated 2-5-1990 in favour of defendant No. 5 in respect of the suit land; the defendant after inquiry of the DIT records and title deed, created a mortgage deed of the suit property as security of the loan which was repayable within one year.

6. Similarly one Anwarul Huq, proprietor of M/s Anwar Trading Co. applied for Muajjal facility of one crore to the defendant No. 5 which was sanctioned on 30-12-1989 against collateral security of equitable mortgage of the suit property of defendant Nos. 1-3 i.e. guarantor of the loan; those loan was also repayable within one year; after sometimes defendant Nos. 1 -3 created equitable and legal mortgage of the suit property in favour of the defendant No. 5 and also executed a registered irrevocable general power of attorney in favour of this defendant No. 5; that the suit property therefore legally and bonafide stands as security of the facilities granted by the defendant No. 5 on the above account; the defendant No. 5 also acted bonafide in creating mortgage of the suit land and being satisfied and after inspecting the title deed and the records of DIT accepted the security as aforesaid and completed all legal formalities: the borrowers, Masud Enterprise and Anwar Trading Co failed to adjust the dues of the answering defendant and for these reasons this defendant filed two separate Mortgage Suits being Title Suit No. 80 of 1992 and 81 of 1992 respectively in the Court of 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka and the court decreed both the suits in preliminary form and thereafter final decree was drawn directing sale of the suit property; this defendant has also filed execution case for sale of the schedule property as per mortgage deed which were pending for disposal; it was also disclosed in the written statement by the defendant No. 5 that the plaintiff has no charge whatsoever over the suit land nor defendant Nos.1-3 executed any mortgage in favour of the plaintiff; it was also disclosed in the writ-ten statement that the attachment order of the court in Money Execution Case filed in 1993 having created no right in favour of the plaintiff as against prior mortgage in favour of answering defendant No. 5; the plaintiff cannot claim first charge on the basis of subsequent attachment against the earlier mortgage charge, therefore, the defendant No. 5 prayed for dismissal of the suit.

7. The suit was eventually taken up for hearing on transfer by the learned Subordinate Judge now the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka; two witnesses one Sheikh Amjad Hossain and another Manik Chandra Das were examined on behalf of the plaintiff in support of its case while two witnesses one on behalf of the defendant Nos. 1-3 and another on behalf of defendant No. 5 were also examined and upon consideration of the evidence and materials placed before the trial court the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Dhaka by his judgment and decree dated 26-11-2001 dismissed the suit on contest and exparte against the non contesting ones; the said judgment and decree dated 26-11-2001 is in challenge before this court in First Appeal No. 142 of 2002.

8. It may be mentioned that the original Title Suit No.280 of 1994 was eventually re-numbered as Title Suit 35 of 2001 on transfer before the learned Joint District Judge and 1st Additional Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka. During pendency of the appeal, on 6-8-2010 one Aminul Huq son of late Lutfor Rahman got himself impleaded as respondent No. 3(a) of this appeal and subsequently on 18-8-2010 Sonali Bank Ltd. got itself added as respondent 3(b) in this appeal.

9. Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 has been brought by Agrani Bank as decree holder petitioner impleading M/s Goldhill Fibers Ltd.; Abidur Rahman as judgment debtor opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, Sonali Bank as 3rd party opposite party No. 3 and Aminul Hoq auction purchaser as opposite party No.4, against order No. 121 dated 20-6-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4 in Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 (re-numbered) staying writ of delivery of possession to be given to the petitioner bank, stating inter alia in the said revisional application as under:- that the petitioner bank as plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 16 of 1985 on 24-6-1985 before the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj for recovery of Taka 31,33,664 against the opposite party Nos.1 and 2; the said suit was decreed ex parte on 5-6-1986; the said decree was put into execution in Money Execution Case No. 71 of 1988 on 9-4-1988 before the Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj; thereafter said decree was sent to the court of District Judge, Dhaka for execution on the basis of no objection certificate; accordingly Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was started on 14-8-1988 before the Sub-ordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka (at present Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka) for recovery of decretal dues amounting to Taka 45,65,182 as on 6-4-1988; the property measuring 14 khatas 15 chataks situated at House No. 33, Block CEN(H) Road No. 114, Gulshan Model Town belonging to the judgment debtor No. 2 Mr Abidur Rahman was included in the schedule of the execution case; after obtaining a contested decree for benami declaration dated 21-4-2002 against three sons of judgment debtor (benamder) in Title Suit No. 190 of 1999 before the Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No.2, Dhaka; the revisional application also contains similar averments as made in the plaint of the Title Suit out of which the instant First Appeal is pending, therefore, skipped over to avoid repetition, it was also stated in the said revisional application that the decree holder petitioner bank on 15-9-2009 filed an application for issuance of writ of delivery of possession of the attached property to the decree holder Agrani Bank since the aforesaid property had already been attached in the execution case brought by the petitioner bank; the said application was allowed by the executing court on 17-11-2009 issued writ of delivery of possession for giving possession to the decree holder fixing 14-1-2010 for service return; thereafter Sonali Bank opposite party No. 3 filed an application on 25-11-2009 for recalling the writ of delivery of possession whereupon the executing court allowed the prayer exparte vide order No. 107 dated 25-11-2009; accordingly writ was recalled; thereafter the petitioner bank as decree holder filed written objection stating inter alia that the property in question could not be sold in auction because of shockingly low price quoted by the bidders, therefore, on the prayer of the decree holder bank a certificate of enjoyment and possession and sale under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 was issued in favour of the decree holder petitioner bank; eventually the writ of delivery of possession was also given in favour of the petitioner bank; thereafter Sonali Bank filed an application for recalling of the delivery of possession which after hearing both sides was allowed by the impugned order maintaining the previous order dated 25-11-2009, therefore, the instant Civil Revision has been brought challenging the said order No. 121 dated 20-6-2010 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka.

10. The opposite party No.3 Sonali Bank entered appearance upon filing a counter affidavit.

11. Civil Revision No. 4762 of 2010 has been brought by Sonali Bank as petitioner impleading Al-Baraka Bank Ltd as decree holder opposite party No. 1, M/s Gold hill Fibers Ltd and Abidur Rahman as judgment debtor opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 Md Aminul Huq auction purchaser as opposite party No. 4 challenging order No. 133 dated 14-10-2010 passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka refusing to cancel the certificate issued earlier in favour of decree holder opposite party No. 1 under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 (previously Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988); the said revisional application by Sonali Bank has been brought stating inter alia that the Sonali Bank allowed loan in favour of opposite party No. 3 Abidur Rahman from London Branch of the Bank but he defaulted in payment of the loan; the Queen's Bench Division of UK decreed the suit in 1984 against him for an amount of 4,14,323.79 sterling/ pound; there was no appeal against the said decree of the Queen's Bench Division. Therefore, it was put to execution as money execution suit No. 23 of 1987 in the 1st Commercial Court, Dhaka since that was a foreign decree; thereafter on a direction from the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 7238 of 1989 execution case was filed before the District Judge, Dhaka; accordingly it was transferred to the court of learned District Judge, Dhaka and was renumbered as Money Execution Case No.2 of 1989; thereafter on 15-10-1990 the said property was attached by the learned District Judge in the said execution case; the judgment debtor Abidur Rahman challenged the order No. 24 dated 15-10-1990 before the High Court Division in Civil Revision which was rejected in Civil Order No.2276 of 1990; the said order was also upheld by the Appellate Division by its judgment and order dated 23-5-1991 passed in Civil Petition No.386 of 1990; thereafter one of the three sons of Abidur Rahman namely, Nowshad Asif filed an application under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992; but after hearing said Miscellaneous Case was rejected on 27-3-1995; against the said order Civil Revision No. 2279 of 1995 was preferred and rule was issued but after hearing the said rule was also discharged on 7-8-1996; the executing court found the decree holder, Abidur Rahman as the owner of the attached property and his three sons are his benamders; the said finding of the executing court was also affirmed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2279 of 1995 against which Nowshad Asif did not prefer any appeal; thereafter Samsad Asif, another son of Abidur Rahman preferred Civil Revision No. 1084 of 1999 challenging an order of the executing court rejecting his prayer for stay of all further proceedings in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 on the plea of pendency of Writ Petition No. 2795 of 1998 and 2796 of 1998 till disposal of execution case No. 58-60 of 1995 arising out of Title Suit Nos. 80 and 81 of 1992 and Title Suit No. 223 of 1998 but after hearing the said rule was eventually discharged by judgment arid order dated 10-3-2002 passed by this Court in Civil Revision No. 1084 of 1999; after discharge of the aforesaid rule the execution case proceeded and the attached property was sold in auction on 10-7-2006 to the auction purchaser Md Aminul Huq, the opposite party No. 4, who purchased the same at Taka 3,11,00,000; he also paid taxes and fees in this connection to the tune of Taka 3,12,000.

12. Challenging the auction sale, Samsad Asif, son of Abidur Rahman, preferred Civil Revision No. 2373 of 2006 while Oriental Bank Ltd. also filed another Civil Revision challenging the said auction sale in Civil Revision No. 3050 of 2006; both the said Civil Revisions were also heard analogously by this court and the rules were discharged by judgment and order dated 5-11-2007 and the said judgment dated 5-11-2007 was also affirmed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal Nos.422 of 2008 and 280 of 2008 by their lord-ships judgment dated 25-3-2009; thereafter execution case No. 2 of 1999 was proceeded and on 3-6-2009 sale certificate was issued, on 8-6-2009 the same was registered in favour of the opposite party No.4 Md Aminul Huq and the writ of delivery of possession was issued by order dated 10-6-2009 in favour of the auction purchaser but due to obstruction created by the judgment debtor possession of the property could not be delivered to the auction purchaser for which he applied for police force and the executing court allowed; meanwhile Samsad Asif filed an application under Order XXI, rule 90 in Miscellaneous Case No. 2 of 2009 before the Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for setting aside the auction sale in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989; similarly, the Agrani Bank also filed a similar application before the same court in Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2009; both the said Miscellaneous Cases were admitted and further proceeding of Money Execution Case was stayed by the learned Additional District Judge by his order dated 18-8-2009; the petitioner Sonali Bank preferred Civil Revision No. 3394 of 2009 and 3982 of 2009 before the High Court Division and obtained rule and stay operation of the said order dated 18-8-2009; and eventually both the rules were made absolute by the High Court Division.

13. In Civil Revision No.3982 of 2009 arising out of Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2009 filed by Agrani Bank Ltd. High Court Division when making the rule absolute on 24-3-2010 directed the executing court to hear the Miscellaneous Case No.3 of 2009 within two weeks on the point of limitation which has been complied by the executing court within time; eventually by its order dated 4-5-2010 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No. 3 of 2009 filed by Agrani Bank on the ground of limitation; against the said order dated 4-5-2010 Agrani Bank preferred FMAT No. 379 of 2010 before this court which was also dismissed by the judgment and order dated 26-7-2010 passed by a Division Bench of this Court; in the meantime the opposite party No. 1, Agrani Bank obtained a money decree against the opposite party Nos.2 and 3 in Money Suit No. 16 of 1985 and eventually brought Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 before the 1st Commercial Court, Dhaka; said execution case was renumbered as Artha Jari Case No.79 of 2010 which has been pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka; in the said Money Execution Case, the land of Tejkunipara mouza was included in the schedule of the case but, subsequently, Agrani Bank Ltd. upon an application under Order VI, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure included the attached land of Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 in Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 on 12-9-2002; thereafter Agrani Bank obtained certificate under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 in respect of the said attached land on 13-11-2004; thereafter on 27-11-2005 Money Execution Case No. 177 of 1988 was finally disposed of; thereafter Samsad Asif son of judgment debtor, Abidur Rahman preferred writ petition No. 448 of 2005 before this Court against order dated 27-11-2005 and two other orders claiming himself as co-owner of the said property; but after hearing of the said writ petition rule was discharged holding that Samsad Asif is not the co-owner of the said property and affirmed the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Ain, 2003 in favour of Agrani Bank; Agrani Bank had knowledge about the attachment of the said property in execution case No.2 of 1989 from 23-6-2002 but knowing about the said attachment of the property they obtained the order of attachment of the said land in Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 on 23-9-2002 and on the basis of such illegal attachment they obtained certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003; Agrani Bank obtained order of delivery of possession of the said property in their favour in Money Execution Case No. 79 of 2010 and the petitioner filed an application for recalling the said order of delivery of possession with a prayer for releasing the property from attachment and for deleting the schedule land from the plaint of the execution case whereupon executing court after hearing the parties by his order dated 20-6-2010 recalled the order of delivery of possession but rejected the prayer for releasing the property from attachment upon holding that since the certificate under section 33(5) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain 2003 has been issued the property is not in attachment, therefore, the same cannot be attached; there-after the petitioner on 30-6-2010 filed another application for cancellation of the said certificate obtained by Agrani Bank stating all the material facts upon filing all necessary papers; the Agrani Bank filed a written objection against the said application dated 20-6-2010 but they did not deny the facts that they brought Miscellaneous Case No. 36 of 2002 for setting aside the exparte decree in Title Suit No.297 of 2001; thereafter the learned Joint District Judge after hearing the parties rejected the said application by his impugned order dated 14-2-2010 which has been challenged in the instant rule.

14. The opposite party No. 1 Agrani Bank entered appearance upon filing a counter affidavit denying the material allegations made in the petition stating inter alia that Agrani Bank allowed loan in favour of opposite party No.2 M/s Goldhill Fibers Ltd. of which the Managing Director was opposite party No. 3 Abidur Rahman; he defaulted in repayment of the loan as such the opposite party No.1 Agrani Bank Limited brought Title Suit No. 16 of 1985 against them for realization of the said loan and eventually suit was decreed against the opposite party Nos. 2 and 3 as such Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was brought by the opposite party No. 1 which was renumbered as Artha Jari Case No. 79 of 2010 which has been pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.4, Dhaka; the said land was included in the schedule of Money Execution Case which was attached thereafter Agrani Bank obtained Certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat AM, 2003 on 30-11-2004; on 27-11-2005 the said Money Execution Case No. 176 of 1988 was disposed of; thereafter one son of Abidur Rahman the judgment debtor namely Samsad Asif preferred Writ Petition No. 448 of 2005 challenging the said order dated 27-1-2005 which after hearing the rule was discharged affirming the certificate issued under section 33(5) in favour of Agrani Bank and subsequently, the opposite-party No. 1 obtained order of delivery of possession of the said property in their favour in Money Execution Case No.79 of 2010; it was also asserted on oath in the said counter affidavit that Sonali Bank Ltd. practiced fraud upon the court beyond the knowledge of opposite party No. 1 and attached the said property in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 filed by the petitioner and was sold in auction on 10-7-2006 to the auction purchaser Md Aminul Huq the opposite party No. 4; thereafter the petitioner filed application for cancellation of the said certificate in favour of the opposite party No. 1 and after hearing the learned Joint District Judge rejected the said application by his order dated 24-10-2010 which has been impugned in the instant rule.

15. Mr ANM Abdur Razzaq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Agrani Bank in First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 submits that the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Adalat No.1 having failed to appreciate the case of the plaintiff appellant, upon misconstruction of the documentary evidence produced by the plaintiff, passed the impugned judgment dismissing the suit which being contrary to the evidence and materials on record is liable to be set aside.

16. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that the findings of the trial court to the effect that “বাদী পক্ষ নালিশী ভূমি বন্ধক রেখেছেন মর্মে প্রমান করতে পারেন নাই এবং নালিশী ভূমিতে ৪ নং বিবাদী পক্ষের স্বত্ব স্বার্থ থাকার বিষয়টিও প্রমাণ করতে পারেন নাই। তাই বাদী পক্ষ আদৌ নালিশী ভূমি দ্বারা ৪ নং বিবাদীর ঋণের জন্য বাদী ব্যাংকের ভেলিড প্রথম চার্জ রয়েছে মর্মে প্রমানিত হয়। এছাড়া যেহেতু নালিশী ভূমিতে ১ হতে ৩ নং বিবাদী গণের ৫ নং বিবাদী ব্যাংকে নালিশী সম্পত্তি বন্ধক দিয়ে ঋণ নিয়েছেন মর্মে প্রমানিত হচ্ছে। being contrary to the evidence and materials on record, dismissal of the suit by the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law.

17. Mr Sayyid Shahid Hossain , the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 5 Al-Baraka Bank Ltd. submits that it has been consistently held by superior courts of the sub-continent that when father or mother purchases the property for benefit of his/her children or husband purchases for the benefit of the wife the transaction is not a benami one but it is a gift.

18. In substantiating his submission to the effect as above, the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in AIR 1923 (Patna) 187.

19. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5, that the ingredients of the Benami transaction as laid down by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 61 DLR (AD) 133 the factum of intention to create benami, possession of property, possession of title deeds having not been raised or decided by the executing court earlier the question of res judicata is not applicable in Title Suit No. 35 of 2001.

20. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5 that the execution having no jurisdiction to decide the issue of title to property or the question of Benami transaction in a proceeding under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure the principle of res judicata is not applicable to Title Suit No. 35 of 2001 filed by Agrani Bank against which the instant appeal has been brought.

21. In substantiating his submissions the-learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in 16 DLR (SC) 287, 54 CWN 372, AIR 1950 (Cal) 342 and 54 DLR 123.

22. The learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5 further submits that the sons of Abidur Rahman being the real owner and the property has been being mortgaged with Al-Baraka since 2-6-1990. The certificate of Agrani Bank under section 33(5) dated 30-11-2004 and attachment of Sonali Bank on 15-10-1990 or 10-7-2006 or sale by tender on 10-7-2006 or sale by tender on 10-7-2006 are void ab initio.

23. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 5 that in case of absence of jurisdiction of the court consent of the party cannot create jurisdiction, therefore, the decision over the ownership in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1992, 3 of 2006, 5 of 2006 filed in Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 under Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure is a nullity and all decisions subsequently in Civil Revision and Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal can be of no avail more particularly when neither in the executing court nor in the High Court Division or before the Appellate Division the question of scope of Order XXI, rule 58 of the Code of Civil Procedure was ever mooted and decided.

24. In substantiating his submissions to the effect as above, the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case reported in 10 DL. R 634, AIR 1958 (All) 636.

25. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Sonali Bank and the auction purchaser added respondent No. 3 and 3(a) submits that Sonali Bank obtained a decree on 28-9-1984 against Abidur Rahman from the Queens Bench Division, England and in executing of the said decree the suit property has been attached on 15-10-1990 in Money Execution Case No. 23 of 1987 re-numbered as Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989.

26. It is also submitted by Mr Mahmudul Islam that Al-Baraka Bank is presumed to know about the existence of said order of attachment from Civil Revision No. 1084 of 1999 filed by Samsad Asif in which Al-Baraka Bank was the opposite party No.2 but it failed to take any step in respect of the said attached property.

27. It is also submitted by the learned Advocate for the added respondent Nos. 3 and 3(a) that on the prayer of Sonali Bank the court attached the property on 15-10-1990, sold the property in auction on 10-7-2006, the auction sale was confirmed on 17-7-2006 but Al-Baraka Bank did not take any step to set aside the sale under the provision of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure.

28. Mr Islam, further submits that a proceeding under Order XXI, rule 58 is not a summary proceeding it should be treated a regular suit. All questions including the question of title and right of the claimants have to be adjudicated, separate suit for decision on title or right is barred.

29. In substantiating his submissions the learned Advocate placed reliance in the case of SS Allois Ltd. vs BM Steel reported in AIR 1978 (Mad) 270.

30. Mr Islam also placed reliance in the case of Kalipada Dey vs Dwiza Pada Das reported in AIR 1930 (PC) 22 to substantiate his submissions that a decision in probate proceeding as to relationship of the owners to property operate as res judicata too.

31. In resolving the aforesaid questions we can safely refer to the latest judgment delivered by the Apex Court in Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 452 of 2012 heard with 634-635 of 2012,2339 of 2011 and 246 of 2012 arising out of judgment and order dated 26-10-2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 analogously with Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 making the rule absolute there-by cancelled the certificate under section 33(5) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 issued in favour of the petitioner Bank.

32. On a careful scrutiny of the aforesaid judgment delivered by the Apex Court in connection with the self-same subject matter involved in this appeal and on scrutiny of the aforesaid judgment passed by the High Court Division and the ultimate decision given by their lordship in the Appellate Division we find that the judgment of the High Court Division though based on the previous decisions of Miscellaneous Cases brought under Order XXI, rule 58 or rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 has been turned down by the Apex Court and the penultimate decision in the aforesaid judgment passed by their lordships reads as under :-

"Judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 and 2755 of 2010 is set aside. Both the Civil Revisions are send back on remand to the High Court Division for hearing afresh along with First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 by a Division Bench presided over by Nozrul Islam Chowdhury, J : within 6 (six) weeks from the date of receipt of this order. However, if so advised, parties may also take step before the concerned Bench for early hearing."

<u>33. From the decision referred to above, it makes it clear that we have to decide the aforesaid cases afresh in accordance with law, therefore, in the context of the submissions made by the learned Advocates from both sides we have addressed ourselves on a question as to whether the proceeding brought earlier steaming up from the execution case No. 2 of 1999 at the instance of Abidur Rahman himself and his three sons which were virtually dragged up to the Apex Court one after another and the question of benami transaction was some way or other decided in those proceedings, should operate as res judicata in the instant appeal or not ?</u>

34. From the facts narrated above, it transpires that Abidur Rahman, the respondent No. 4, obtained loan from the Sonali Bank UK Branch and when he defaulted in repayment of the loan, Sonali Bank obtained a decree in 1984 from the Queens Bench Division of UK against Abidur Rahman and in execution of the said decree Money Execution Case No. 23 of 1987 was initiated in the 1st Commercial Court, Dhaka. Since that was a foreign decree out of which Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 arose upon its transfer to the learned District Judge, Dhaka as per direction of this Court in Civil Revision No.7238 of 1989 and in that execution case said property was attached by the learned District Judge on 15-10-1990.

35. On the other hand, Al-Baraka Bank got the self same land mortgaged in its favour through the respondent Nos. 1-3 in the First Appeal on 2-6-1990 whereupon Mortgage Suit No. 80 of 1992 and 81 of 1992 were brought by Al-Baraka Bank against the guarantor of the loan granted by Al-Baraka Bank. The said suits were also decreed finally and after such decree two execution cases were also brought in 1993 by Al-Baraka Bank and in the said execution case the said property was also attached.

36. Similarly, Agrani Bank having granted loan in favour of Abidur Rahman but he defaulted in repayment of the loan, eventually Money Suits were brought by the Agrani Bank which were also decreed and in execution of those decrees the said property was again attached.

<u>37. In this connection it may be pointed out that the said property was mortgaged in favour of Al-Baraka Bank on 2-6-1990 by defendant Nos. 1-3 (sons of Abidur Rahman) and Sonali Bank got the same land attached in its execution cases on 15-10-1990 while Agrani Bank also got the same land attached in execution of its case on 12-1-2001 and in view of the position as above, we find that the registered mortgage deed obtained by Al-Baraka Bank in respect of the self same land took place earliest in point of time and attachment of the Sonali Bank comes in the 2nd position and the attachment made by Agrani Bank falls in the 3rd position. We have also noticed that Al-Baraka Bank obtained the deed of mortgage in respect of the said property from the ostensible owners thereof as guarantor to the loan granted in favour of two companies both by legal mortgage and by equitable mortgage upon depositing all original deeds in respect of the property to the custody of the said bank. We have also noticed that Al-Baraka Bank has taken all reasonable care and caution to ascertain that the defendant Nos. 1-3 had power to make the mortgage as such Al-Baraka had acted in good faith therefore the mortgage in favour of Al-Baraka Bank by defendant Nos. 1-3 is no doubt protected by section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act. We are of the opinion that the question posed as above, lost its efficacy particularly in view of the fact that the judgment of the said two civil revisions namely Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 and Civil Revision No. 2755 of 2010 passed by the High Court Division complying the principle of res judicata were set aside by their lordships in the Appellate Division in their aforesaid judgment and in the context aforesaid Al-Baraka Bank cannot but be treated as a secured creditor.</u>

38. Now comes the charge over the same property obtained by Sonali Bank on 15-10-1990 by way of attachment thereof in Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 there also admittedly Abidur Rahman the defendant No. 4 was a defaulter of loan and he was adjudicated as judgment debtor, therefore, the execution case was pending against him and the said property eventually was attached in the said proceedings. In this connection it may also be pointed out that Sonali Bank got the said land attached in connection with the loan granted earlier by it to Abidur Rahman from England but in that case Sonali Bank remained an un-secured creditor for the loan granted in favour of Abidur Rahman, since Abidur Rahman was granted loan in his personal capacity and not with reference to any collateral security.

39. It is also not denied by any one that Agrani Bank also granted loan in favour of Abidur Rahman or in favour of the companies of which Abidur Rahman was the Managing Director and in the Money Suit Abidur Rahman was also adjudicated as a judgment debtor when the money suit was brought by Agrani Bank and in course of execution case brought by Agrani Bank the same property was attached on 12-1-2001 last in point of time, therefore, fact remains Abidur Rahman and his three sons all of them are judgment debtors in the aforesaid Money Suits brought by Sonali Bank, Al-Baraka Bank as well as Agrani Bank, therefore, the episode continues till date and the same property once mortgaged by its ostensible owners in favour of Al-Baraka Bank subsequently attached by the Sonali Bank treating its owner Abidur Rahman defendant No. 4, and lastly Agrani Bank has also got the same land attached in the execution case brought by them treating the land belonging to Abidur Rahman the defendant No. 4.

40. We have also noticed that in the loan granted in favour of Abidur Rahman by Sonali Bank, UK Branch there was no reference of the said land in obtaining the loan. Similarly, loan granted by Agrani Bank in favour of two companies belonged to Abidur Rahman there was no reference of the said land but it is only in respect of Al-Baraka Bank, the said land was directly mortgaged by its ostensible owners and the Bank received the mortgage upon exercising due care and caution.

<u>41. In the context of the bizarre episode cropped up herein while deciding the dispute between the parties finally and effectually, we are of the considered opinion that loan obtained from all the three banks which are public money should be redeemed and in doing so the auction sale took place in Money Execution case No. 2 of 1989 cannot be sustained simply because the bid was accepted at a shockingly low price. Similarly, the auction purchaser who has also invested his good money presumably on good faith should also be redeemed duly as far as is practicable, therefore, auction sale took place in Money Execution Case No. 2 of 1989 is hereby set aside.</u>

42. Under the circumstances discussed above and in the context of episode involved herein, we find that we can take recourse to the provision of section 63 of the Code of Civil Procedure which reads as under:-

"63(1)-Where property not in the custody of any Court is under attachment in execution of decrees of more Courts than one, the Court which shall receive or realize such property and shall determine any claim thereto and any objection to the attachment thereof shall be the Court of highest grade or, where there is no difference in grade between such Courts, the Courts under whose decree the property was first attached.

(2) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to invalidate any proceeding taken by a Court executing one of such decrees."

43. Therefore, the Executing Court, 1st Additional District Judge, Dhaka is hereby directed to put the said property in auction with full compliance of the legal formalities and the sale proceeds received out of such sale should be distributed to Al-Baraka Bank at the 1st point of time with 10% interest starting from the date of its Mortgage decree in respect of the loan since it is found to be the only secured creditor.

44. Secondly, the balance amount of the sale proceed shall be paid to Sonali Bank from the date of its attachment of the said property on 15-10-1990 together with interest @ 10% from 15-10-1990, of course Sonali Bank shall adjust its received amount with its auction purchaser, the respondent No. 3a, of this appeal namely Md Aminul Hoque and thereafter the remaining balance amount of the sale proceed shall be paid to Agrani Bank in respect of its decreetal amount together with 10% interest from the date of its attachment on 12-1-2001 and thereafter surplus amount, if any, shall go to the heirs of late Abidur Rahman since he is no more in this world as he died on 12-10-2012.

45. In the process of distribution it may be pointed out further that the first payment shall be made to Al-Baraka Bank, second payment to be made to Sonali Bank which shall redeem its auction purchaser and lastly to Agrani Bank.

46. It may not be out of place to mention that in view of the resolute directions given above we refrain from evaluating the applicability of the decisions cited by the learned Advocates with a view to avoid a mere academic discourse.

47. Turning to the merit of the First Appeal No. 142 of 2002 and the connected two Civil Revisions namely CR No. 2755 of 2010 and Civil Revision No. 4769 of 2010 it may be pointed out further that we have gone through the impugned judgment and on perusal of the judgment passed in Title Suit No.35 of 2001 we find that it is a well reasoned judgment passed on consideration of the evidence and materials placed before the learned Joint District Judge and Additional Artha Rin Court No. 1, Dhaka and the learned Judge meticulously considered the evidence both oral and documentary upon arriving at a positive finding to substantiate the impugned judgment and consequent decree, therefore, it call for no interference by this court. Hence we find no merit in this appeal.

48. So far as those two civil revisions are concerned we find that the rules issued in those revisions have lost their efficacy in view of the ultimate directions given upon the executing court in this instant judgment referred to above, therefore, both the rules in the aforesaid Civil Revision stand disposed of.

49. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs and the connected two Civil Revision Nos. 2755 of 2010 and CR No. 4769 of 2010 are hereby disposed of.

Send down the lower court records with a copy of this judgment, at once for compliance.

End.
